Title: Status and Prospects of the Korean Economy
text: 2006 KRX Listed Companies Expo Keynote Status and Prospects of the Korean Economy 2006. 11. 2. Bank of Korea Governor Lee Sung-tae (Greetings) Mr. Lee Young-tak, Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Korea Stock Futures Exchange, and to domestic and foreign institutional investors and entrepreneurs! Last year's second largest event in the country . I am very pleased to speak at the "2006 KRX Listed Company Expo". We expect that this event will be an opportunity to further enhance our understanding of Korean companies and the Korean economy, which is becoming increasingly of interest to foreign institutional investors, along with the acceleration of global economic and financial integration. Today, from a medium-term perspective, I would like to speak about the changes in the Korean economy since the foreign exchange crisis and the prospects for the future. (Changes in the Korean economy after the foreign exchange crisis) As you well know, the Korean economy experienced an unparalleled event in 1997 called the foreign exchange crisis. However, in a relatively short period of time thereafter , it will be Successfully overcame and was born with a new look. Although there are still many challenges for the Korean economy to solve, I can tell you that the framework of the Korean economy has improved dramatically since before and after the foreign exchange crisis. First, 'competition and efficiency' has become the dominant paradigm in the public sector, not to mention the private sector. Before the foreign exchange crisis, the Korean economy was in fact operating under the protection and regulation of the government. However, as the size of the economy has grown and the structure has become more complex, this method of economic operation has been pushed to the limit due to the so-called high cost and low efficiency. Accordingly, the government has moved away from the protection and regulatory system and implemented extensive institutional reforms to establish a system of autonomous competition in the private sector. At the same time, by intensely promoting financial and corporate restructuring, the principle of survival of the fittest has gradually taken root. Companies have shifted their management from a quantitative growth strategy through increased input of external vehicles and production factors to a direction that attaches importance to qualitative growth through internal management and productivity improvement. There were also difficulties in overcoming the painful pain of restructuring until a new economic paradigm was established, but this was an inevitable choice for the Korean economy to survive under the wave of globalization. Let's do it. Next, the economic constitution has become stronger than it was before the foreign exchange crisis. As Korea's financial industry has gone through the process of brushing off its insolvency and consolidating it, its health has been greatly enhanced, and its profitability and productivity have improved markedly. For example, the BIS capital health ratio of general banks has risen from 7.0% at the end of 1997 to 12.4% at the end of 2005 , and the ROA ratio has also risen from -1.06% in 1997 to 1.24% in 2005 , which is close to the level of developed countries. The financial structure of Korean companies has also become very strong. As of the end of 2005, manufacturers have a debt ratio of 101%, which is only one-fourth of the 396% at the end of 1997 , which is lower than that of U.S. or Japanese companies. In addition, major industries such as semiconductors, shipbuilding, steel, and automobiles, in particular , are gaining global competitiveness. In addition, with the expansion of the opening up of the domestic market, various competition-restrictive regulations have been eliminated, and corporate governance and management transparency have also been improved to a level that is in line with global standards. South Korea's foreign exchange reserves are at 2,282 billion as of the end of September this year, and the country's credit rating has recovered to near-pre-crisis levels. Based on this improvement in constitution, the macroscopic performance achieved by the Korean economy is also generally good. Since the beginning of 2003, the card debt bubble in the household sector has been extinguished, resulting in a domestic recession of just over two years , but since domestic demand revived in the second quarter of last year, private consumption and equipment investment have continued to grow steadily to date. Over the six years from 2000 to 2005, somewhat relieved of the shock of the foreign exchange crisis, the average annual GDP growth rate was 5.1%, which is by no means a low level in light of the stage of development of a country's economy. My Korean economy ranks 11th in the world in terms of size. The performance on the waterfront is even more remarkable. As you are well aware, in the past , the Korean economy suffered a lot of difficulties due to the high inflation rate, which is why price stability was one of the most important policy tasks. However, since the foreign exchange crisis, the rate of inflation has been significantly lower. The average annual rate of consumer inflation fell from 8.4% in the 1980s and 6.1% in 1990-97 to 3.2% in 2000-04 . Since 2005, it has fallen to 2%. In the 2000s, the sharp slowdown in the rise in prices was largely due to the fact that in addition to the relatively low domestic market, the increase in the value of the won, the expansion of imports of low-cost consumption goods, and the progress of distribution innovation were also largely due to the increase in the value of the yuan . Everything. In addition, the fact that the Bank of Korea's price stability target system has been established and the significant decline in inflation is also considered to have contributed to price stability. The Gyeongsang Water Index has continued to see a large black tide driven by a solid increase in exports. Since it was converted into a surplus in 1998, just after the foreign exchange crisis, it has recorded a total surplus of 824 billion by last year. During 1-9 January of this year, the current balance of funds showed a slight deficit due to the large rise in international oil prices and the deterioration of the service balance, but the export boom continues, and oil prices have also been showing stable movements in recent years, which is expected to indicate a slight surplus for the entire year. . The financial market was temporarily agitated by the insolvency of credit card companies in 2003, but has remained generally stable since 2004. The long-term indicator rate on the basis of the 3-year Treasury bond circulation yield has been moving steadily since 2004 at a generally 4% range. Stock prices have been on an upward trend since the beginning of 2005 due to the improvement of the real economy and the expansion of the stock demand base. The delinquency rate of bank credit card companies, which reached 8.4% at the end of 2003, has recently plummeted to around 2%, and the delinquency rate of bank loans has continued to be as low as 1%, resulting in significant credit risks in the household and corporate sectors. It shows that it has decreased. Meanwhile, financial institutions are steadily increasing their supply of funds to the household and SMEs in response to the low demand for funds from large companies due to their abundant liquidity reserves. (Future Prospects) In recent years, some people have raised concerns about the Korean economy. As the expansion of the domestic economy slows down, and the uncertainty caused by the North Korean nuclear test crisis increases, it is true that in the short term, the downside risk to the economy is higher than it was in the past. However, from a medium- to long-term perspective, we are confident that the Korean economy will continue to grow at a similar level to that of 2000-05. These plates are based on the following points: First, as I mentioned earlier, the Korean economy now has a significant amount of domestic and international shock absorption . Above all, the health and stability of the financial industry has been dramatically improved, and the scale has also been greatly expanded. As of the end of 2005, the total asset capital of the deposit bank was 1,200 trillion won, more than twice as large as the 570 trillion won at the end of 1997, just before the foreign exchange crisis. The size of the capital market has increased fivefold, from 300 trillion won at the end of 1997 to 1,500 trillion won at the end of 2005. Since May of this year , foreign investors have been selling their shares in large numbers during portfolio adjustments, but the stock price has continued its upward trajectory. The share of foreign equity investments reached 35.5% at the end of September 2006, despite the large sell-offs. In the wake of the North Korean nuclear test in early October, stock prices, interest rates, and exchange rates showed the strength to stabilize in the short term . The corporate sector has also made significant improvements in its financial structure and international competitiveness, and the expansion of foreign exchange reserves and the securing of financial health also support confidence in the country's economy. Second, the ROK Government's multi-faceted initiatives to expand its growth potential are being pursued, and these efforts will be further strengthened in the future. At present, the ROK Government recognizes the expansion of growth potential as the most urgent policy task and plans to create a "good environment for business" by formulating various regulations that hinder corporate investment. In addition, we continue to expand the scope of external openness, increasing the competitiveness of the relatively backward service industry, and taking effective measures to make the leap to the financial hub of Northeast Asia. Third, Korean companies have been able to afford to invest well through improved profits and stable management. Cash Reserves of Korean Companies The percentage has risen from 6.4% at the end of 1997 to 10.0% at the end of 2005, and the wealth debt ratio is also very low compared to the world's major corporations. In addition, the technical skills of Korean companies are also at a high level. GDPcontrast R&D Investment Proportion world 9 Level As Known You. Lee and Lee The same superior Technology enterprise  adequate Investment Ability and If combined Korean Economy The growth is Further Increase will. Finally, let me briefly talk about the Bank of Korea's monetary policy. The Bank of Korea will continue to operate its policy in a way that keeps prices stable and pays attention to economic trends. We will not neglect to secure the basis for price stability at the level of developed countries and to maintain the stability of the financial system. We will keep a close eye on changes in economic conditions at home and abroad, closely analyze their impact on the financial market and the real economy , and respond proactively. In addition, we will strengthen communication with the gold financing market to increase the predictability of monetary policy, while also performing the central bank's financial stability function more faithfully by checking for potential market disturbances at all times and responding quickly if necessary. (Conclusion) Dear investors and entrepreneurs at home and abroad! I would like to remind you once again that the future of the Korean economy is still bright. Of course, in the short term, amid concerns about a slowdown in the economy , there are also long-term challenges such as deepening imbalances between sectors and the rigidity of the labor market. However, the Korean economy has wisely overcome numerous crises over the past 40 years. Many economists around the world have not hesitated to cite South Korea as a prime example of how they have successfully overcome the crisis through continuous reforms. The strength of the Korean economy has been accumulated in the process of responding dynamically to the crisis , which we believe is the greatest asset to the Korean economy in making the leap to the advanced economy . Finally, I would like to thank all the people who have invited Chairman Lee Yong-tak to be here today, and I wish the event a success and the development of the IR Expo as Asia's flagship IR Expo. Thank you for listening.

(attached) Commemorative speech for the 57th anniversary of its founding 2007. 6. 12 Bank of Korea President Lee Sung-tae Dear Bank of Korea Family! Today marks the 57th anniversary of the Bank of Korea's first steps as the central bank of our country. First of all, I would like to express my deepest gratitude to the many people who have lent this position and have given encouragement and advice for the development of the Bank of Korea from its inception until today. I would also like to congratulate you for the hard work of our employees who are faithfully performing their duties in their respective positions. This year, our economy has shown a movement in which exports continue to grow at a high rate and domestic demand improves. While prices remain stable , the rise in real estate prices has also slowed, and the current water supply has recorded a slight deficit. In view of such an economic situation, the party has operated a monetary policy with a focus on ensuring that the trend of improvement of the real water economy continues , while paying attention to price stability. Under this policy framework, we have maintained the 4.5% annual call rate target that was adjusted for the increase in August last year. At the same time, in response to the fact that the monetary growth rate has continued at a high level due to the large increase in loans to financial institutions, we have also made policy efforts to curb the growth of liquidity. In particular, in order to make the effect of the measures to increase the reserve rate implemented at the end of last year visible, the bank has induced the management of funds with theft through open market manipulation. Going forward, our economy is expected to be able to achieve growth in the mid-4% range this year with a somewhat faster recovery. Prices will continue to stabilize both consumer prices and source inflation, and the current water supply is expected to be largely balanced. However, since there is not much uncertainty in foreign factors such as the rise in the price of international commodities and the possibility of instability in the international gold financing market, it is necessary to examine this matter closely. Han Eun Family! Recently , the domestic and international conditions surrounding monetary policy have been changing rapidly, and we must intensify our efforts to respond to this. First, as the integration of domestic and foreign financial markets accelerates, the flow of international finance is having a great impact on the domestic financial market. In particular, with the emergence of various derivatives financing, the ripple path of monetary policy is becoming uncertain . Domestically, there has been a stinging phenomenon such as the expansion of competitive loans by financial institutions, which is putting a strain on the operation of monetary policy. Such a sting may be inevitable from the point of view of individual economic actors, but in the overall volume of the national economy, it can have undesirable consequences, such as excessive expansion of the liquidity supply and increased possibility of market instability. In the meantime, there have also been concerns that the rapid growth of household debt, mainly on mortgages, could reduce the elastic operating room of monetary policy due to the deterioration of households' ability to repay debt . Fortunately, although the growth of mortgages has slowed this year, it is difficult to expect an early improvement in the financial structure of households in light of the fact that individuals' net savings rates continue to be at a low level. The short-term development of the post-foreign exchange crisis cycle is another challenge to consider when it comes to the operation of monetary policy. As the economic cycle is shortened due to the restructuring of the export structure to the center of IT products, which do not have a large industrial related effect, and the contraction of equipment investment due to the remuneration of corporate management, the effect of monetary policy is likely to be different from the original expectations. In order to maintain the effectiveness of monetary policy in such a situation, it is first of all necessary to have the ability to accurately analyze and predict the changes in the situation in the financial markets at home and abroad and their ramifications. Aul In line with changes in the economic structure of Russia, efforts should also be made to improve the policy analysis framework and re-examine the effects of sectoral policy waves, in order to improve the real-world fit of monetary policy. Han Eun Family! Now, let me tell you about the issues that the Bank of Korea should pursue with emphasis after the second half of the year. Interest rate policy should be operated with a comprehensive consideration of the economy, financial market conditions, and asset price trends, while paying attention to price stability. In particular, the recent high liquidity growth may act as inflationary pressure in the medium to long term, so we should pay more attention to the movement of monetary indicators. In addition, we should evaluate the operating performance of the interest rate target system and take measures to improve the price function of the call rate while keeping the call rate stable at the policy target level. It is also necessary to improve the monetary policy management unit in the direction of promoting open market manipulation and the linkage of lending and holding systems. We should also do more to increase policy transparency and predictability, such as opening the announcement of the direction of monetary policy. Financial stability efforts should also be strengthened. There is a potential for insecurity in the international financial markets, and a stinging phenomenon is emerging domestically. We will have to closely monitor the movements of the financial markets at home and abroad, and if any abnormal signs are detected, we will have to deal with them quickly through open market manipulation. At the same time, as there is a possibility that non-bank financial institutions that handle payment settlement business will be expanded, we should make every effort to ensure the safety of the payment system. The next-generation Haneun Financial Network System District, scheduled for operation in 2009 Efforts to increase the efficiency of the payment system, such as promoting the axis work without a hitch, should also be continued. With the issuance of the new banknote last time, we have all been able to reaffirm the people's high interest in money. In order to ensure that the issuance of high-value notes, which are targeted for the first half of 2009, can be carried out as scheduled, a comprehensive plan covering the entire process from the article to the issuance of banknotes should be carefully formulated and pursued without error. In response to the growing social interest in rational economic behavior in the national economic education , we must strengthen targeted education and continue to develop a variety of content. The efficient operation of foreign currency assets should also require a distribution effort. In order to increase profitability while ensuring liquidity and safety, we must diversify our investment targets and politicize our investment techniques. There is also a need to explore ways to make more active use of foreign exchange reserves, such as currency swap confirmations. Han Eun Family! It should be borne in mind that under a market economy, monetary policy can only achieve the desired policy effect if the people's trust in the central bank is backed up, and this trust of the people can only be implemented on the basis of excellent ability and strict self-management. First of all, we must strengthen the function of the investigation policy to more accurately assess and determine the future economic situation and have the ability to respond to timely political measures. Through smooth information exchange between departments and active policy discussions, the capacity of the entire organization should be multiplied. In addition, we must establish an early establishment of a personnel salary system based on competence and sexuality, and eliminate the wasteful elements of the budget to further improve the efficiency of management. Last year, the Bank of Korea prepared the "Medium- and Long-Term Development Strategy" and the "Management Innovation Plan" and has been promoting them in a full-fledged manner. We should all share the awareness and actively participate in the idea that such self-innovation is the best option for the development of the party. Dear Bank of Korea Family! We are now living in an era where the speed of change dictates competitiveness. Employees should face this and not settle for today , but be proactive in preparing for tomorrow ahead of others. In addition, we should always be aware of the fact that we are public servants who are in charge of the lives of the people. Even in the midst of difficult working conditions, when we unwaveringly make concerted efforts to fulfill our duties, the people's trust in the Bank of Korea will be strengthened. On the occasion of our 57th anniversary, we once again express our deepest gratitude for your hard work and wish you and your families good health and happiness. Thanks. 06/ 12/2007 Governor Sung Tae

Title: Opening of the 17th Central Banking Seminar
text: Opening of the 17th Central Bank Seminar Opening Remarks 2009. 10. 20 Bank of Korea Governor Lee Sung-tae ( Greetings )  Organized by the Bank of Korea Countries that attended the Central Banking Seminar Welcoming Central Bank Employees  Mr. Jean-Pierre Landau will also give a special lecture in a few moments. I would also like to express my deep gratitude to the Vice-Governor of the Bank of France .  Celebrating its seventeenth anniversary this year, the seminar is designed to share the diverse experience and knowledge of central banks in each country on key issues of monetary policy and to broaden the exchange between employees.  In particular, the theme of this seminar , "Response and Challenges" Global Financial Crisis : Central Bank Policy It is a common concern of all central banks that are trying to wisely overcome the global financial crisis and achieve sustainable growth. ( Global Financial Crisis and Central Bank Policy Response )  For central banks, the global financial crisis is seen as the biggest challenge . After the Great Depression of the 1930s  As the global low-price, low-interest rate trend has been going on for a long time, imbalances in the financial sector have accumulated at a more severe level than ever before, so the impact of the crisis that results from this is just as great.  With the great progress in the globalization of finance and the economy, the crisis triggered by the United States is rapidly transitioning to countries around the world.  Developed countries , as well as emerging markets in Asia, where macroeconomic conditions were relatively good at the time of the crisis, immediately faced great difficulties.  As the crisis spreads through direct and non-bank financial institutions, which have become significantly more important than in the past , Central banks, which have traditionally had a bank-centric policy and management system, have found it difficult to quickly identify and systematically respond to changes in the situation.  Due to these characteristic factors of the financial crisis, the response policies of the central banks of each country that have responded to them have also changed significantly from those of the past.  In response to the severity of the crisis, central banks in major countries have cut policy rates significantly in a short period of time, with some combining quantitative easing or credit easing policies.  In addition to banks, various policies are introduced that directly target non-bank financial institutions or individual financial markets.  In the process of crisis response , the central banks of each country actively participate in policy coordination.  Simultaneous policy rate cuts after the Lehman crisis, Currency swap system between central banks Tightening of medicines is a prime example of this. ( Lessons from the Financial Crisis and Policy Challenges )  Thanks to the rapid and bold policy response of governments and central banks, the global financial market is finding stability and the real economy is showing a recovery centered on emerging market countries .  Looking back on the past period at a time when the world economy is at its worst, the central bank has learned a number of lessons from this crisis.  As the long-accumulated imbalances in the financial sector have been a major cause of this crisis, it is very important to adjust the monetary policy framework in a timely manner to the changes in the financial situation in order to prevent a recurrence of the crisis.  In order to do this, it is necessary to pay more attention than ever before to the credit situation and asset price movements in policy decisions.  On the other hand, it is also important to note that the unusual financial easing measures taken in the course of the crisis response do not lead to another imbalance in the medium-term clock.  The need for central banks to perform the traditional lender of last resort function and the function of a market maker of last resort to resolve credit crunches in individual or the entire financial market is also increasing.  However, in the process, it is necessary to take more thorough measures to prevent the moral hazard of market participants and the exposure of credit risk by central banks .  Due to the globalization of finance and the economy, the policy capabilities of one country alone cannot effectively cope with the crisis, so it is also an important task to consolidate the policy cooperation system between central banks. ( Conclusion )  In this seminar, a serious discussion will be held on the causes of the global financial crisis, the response of each country's policy to the situation, and the challenges ahead. It is hoped that this will provide a number of constructive measures to effectively overcome the crisis and prevent its recurrence.  Finally, although it is a short period of time, we hope that through the fellowship of the participants, the foundation of cooperation between the Sino-Bank Bank will be further consolidated. I hope that even in the midst of a busy schedule, it will be an opportunity to feel the charm of Korean culture and the autumn mood. The 17th Central Banking Seminar The 17th Central Banking Seminar Opening Address October 20, 2009 Seongtae Lee Governor The Bank of Korea ( Opening remarks ) Ladies and Gentlemen, Let me extend a hearty welcome to all central bank staff gathered here from around the world, to take part in the Bank of Korea's "Central Banking Seminar". I should also like to express my deep gratitude to Mr. Jean-Pierre Landau, Deputy Governor of the Bank of France, who will be delivering the keynote address shortly. This seminar, now in its seventeenth year, is held to allow the sharing of diverse experiences and ideas about major monetary policy issues. At the same time, we hope it serves to broaden relationships among central bankers. The theme of this year's seminar, "The Global Financial Crisis: Central Banks' Policy Responses and Challenges", is one of common interest to all central bankers, as they strive to overcome the crisis wisely and achieve sustainable growth. ( The global financial crisis and central banks' policy responses ) As we all know, the current global financial crisis is the most serious challenge to central banks since the Great Depression of the 1930s. Against a background of globally low inflation and low interest rates over some length of time, substantial financial sector imbalances had built up to an extent never before seen. That is why the shock generated by the crisis was so severe. In a situation in which economic and financial globalization has advanced greatly, after the crisis broke out in the U.S., it spread rapidly around the world. And it was therefore not just the advanced countries that suffered. Asian emerging countries, whose macroeconomic conditions were relatively sound, suddenly found themselves in great difficulties as well. The panic was moreover transmitted largely through the direct financial markets and non-bank financial institutions, whose importance has increased greatly in recent years. Central banks, whose policy operations have traditionally focused on commercial banks, therefore had big problems in quickly grasping the evolving situation and developing a systematic response. Owing to these distinctive features of the crisis, the policy initiatives employed by central banks to tackle it have also taken very different forms from in the past. In response to the extreme nature of the crisis, central banks in major countries cut their policy rates by large margins within a short period of time. Some of them also implemented 'quantitative easing' or 'credit easing'. A raft of policies was also introduced that directly addressed non-bank financial institutions or individual financial markets, in addition to commercial banks. In the course of dealing with the crisis, policy cooperation among central banks has also been substantially reinforced. Prominent examples of this were the simultaneous lowering of policy rates and the currency swap agreements among central banks following the collapse of Lehman Brothers. ( Lessons from the financial crisis and policy tasks ahead ) Ladies and Gentlemen, Helped by the prompt and bold policy initiatives of governments and central banks, global financial markets have regained a degree of stability, and the real economy, too, is showing signs of recovery, especially in emerging countries. Looking back over the past months today, now that the world economy seems to have escaped the worst of the crisis, I think there are a number of lessons we central bankers should have learned from this experience. As I mentioned earlier, the financial imbalances accumulated over many years were one major cause of this crisis. To prevent repetition of the crisis, therefore, it seems essential that we carry out more timely adjustments of our monetary policy stances, in line with changes in financial conditions. When making our monetary policy decisions, we must exercise much more vigilance than in the past on credit conditions and asset prices movements. Meanwhile, keen attention should also be paid to ensure that the unprecedentedly bold monetary easing policies adopted to cope with the crisis, do not themselves lead to another set of imbalances in the medium term. There is a growing necessity also that the central bank play not only its traditional role as lender of last resort, but also act as market maker of last resort. By assuming this role as well, we can resolve credit crunches in the individual financial markets or in the financial market as a whole. In order to do this, however, we also need more comprehensive efforts to prevent moral hazard among market participants, and central bank exposure to credit risk. In addition, we have to realize that no one country today has the capacity to tackle a crisis efficiently alone, given the globalization of finance and the economy. Accordingly, building up a robust framework for policy cooperation among central banks is also a very important task. ( Closing remarks ) Fellow central bankers, I am sure that this seminar will provide an opportunity for earnest discussion of the causes of the global financial crisis, of the policy responses taken in each country, and of the tasks ahead. I also hope it will lead to many constructive proposals for efficiently overcoming the crisis and preventing any future repetition of it. Drawing my remarks to a close, let me express my wish that this seminar, although short, may contribute to stronger cooperation by fostering good fellowship among all participants. I hope as well that, despite your jam-packed schedules, you will all have an opportunity to savor the lure of Korean culture and the delights of this beautiful autumn season. Thank you.

Title: New Employee Entrance Ceremony Lethal
text: 2012 New Employee Entrance Ceremony Lethal On behalf of all the employees of the Bank of Korea, we sincerely welcome all the new employees entering the country today to become members of the Bank of Korea's family. I would also like to express to the family and friends who attended this meeting that I am very pleased to celebrate the future of the young people who have become employees of the Bank of Korea since today. Over the course of a lifetime, there are many opportunities that can be a turning point in your life. Perhaps the time to go to school to get an education is the one, the next time to get married and have a family, and in the case of a man, the other important occasion is to go to the military . will be. What is indispensable here is the opportunity to get a job. Although some of the employees who enter the company today have previous work experience, in most cases, the Bank of Korea will be their first job. A very memorable day for new employees will be today when they start their working lives. For the Bank of Korea, today is the 2012 Commencement Ceremony and a very auspicious day for the arrival of a new family member into our organization. I hope that what the Bank of Korea should do as a central bank, especially in the midst of the great uncertainty of the international financial situation in the global economy, the challenges we are going to tackle have already been well communicated to you through the Governor's New Year's Address at the Commencement Ceremony this morning. I hope that in the future, by reading the New Year's Address more times and interpreting its meaning, new employees will be able to know for themselves what to think about and what to do. At this moment, on the occasion of a meaningful induction ceremony, I would like to share with you three things that I believe will be necessary and helpful for me to succeed in my professional life at the Bank of Korea as governor. Rather than the customary virtues of an auspicious day, it can be said that it is a request that each of you conveys in the future of your professional life, hoping that each of you will keep it deep in your heart. The first is to quickly establish a work discipline as a worker, that is, a work discipline. First of all, you should know that this is not a school. In school, people of similar characteristics of the same age lived their lives, and it was also a virtue of being well taught and studying faithfully. It was the school where someone predetermined what you should do. This is a workplace, so there are a lot of different people living there, so you have to have your share of contributions. You need to develop your own work on what you need to do. It's important to do your job well as your organization dictates, but it's just a requirement and not a good enough condition to be a good worker. You need to develop traits that allow you to differentiate yourself. Just as a product that is not differentiated in the market is not sold, so if you do not differentiate yourself from others in the workplace, the utility of the individual will not be great. Of course, there are things that organizations do as they practice, but we must not forget that new ideas are always required for an organization to develop. Since you will be in charge of intellectual rather than physical work, rather than the practice of thinking and acting collectively, you must make contributions based on the ease with which each person can differentiate himself from others. That type of work behavior is to be expected. This requires creativity and a concerted effort to develop your abilities. The general thing you have in common is that you have studied well in a good school. that However, being good at studying only indicates that you are doing a given task well , but it often does not indicate that you have the ability to develop creatively. Moreover, it is yesterday's work that I have done well in my studies, and yesterday is already the past and history. Tomorrow is to create a new one and move on. Even for a moment, I have to keep asking myself if my time like this is worth the remuneration. It is necessary for the development of the organization, but it is also necessary for the development of yourself. Otherwise, you will quickly become indolent and over time, you will develop bad habits of working in such a way that your body will be infiltrated. You have to make a habit of imposing very strict work conditions on yourself and constantly asking if I am a necessary person for this job. The second is to have high dreams, high goals, and a high degree of pride as a central bank employee. There is not much in the world that a person who does not dream and whose goals are low will achieve. Also, there will not be much in this world that can be achieved by those who have no self-esteem and who are always willing to blame others or the environment for what is wrong, or who are willing to rely on others. One of the most heart-wrenching words left by Steve Jobs, the founder of Apple, who passed away not so long ago , is the expression " a toast for the madmen." To make an achievement without falling short of anything means that it is hard to imagine. It is an expression that can absolutely impress young people. Because it is difficult to be crazy about work when you are older, being crazy about work is a privilege that only young people can enjoy. There is of course the expression atmospheric chronic, but those who have done great things that you admire in all walks of life are usually people who went crazy at work when they were young. Coming into a very large organization that is well established, such as the Bank of Korea, it tends to be easily assimilated into the organization and difficult to seize the opportunity to express individual characteristics , so we place a special emphasis on the importance of being at work . will. Maybe there are a number of people who have no aspirations and prefer to live an easy life. Of course, you can live your life that way in this organization, but in the eyes of people like Steve Jobs , it's no different than living your life the way others think . Because the practices of the organization are created by someone else, not me? Isn't it true that you have to make practices so that you can live your lives according to your will? I would like to point out that if you don't build up that kind of strength when you're young, you'll spend your life unwilling . You have to recognize that you must strive to be the protagonist of your life. If you do not make that commitment today , there is a risk that your opportunity to achieve it will be lost , so I am here to awaken your thoughts. Third, we must be proud to be an employee of a central bank. What is the hallmark of living as a central bank employee? There is only one central bank in any country. There is no subject of non-teaching in the country. For you, government officials cannot be directly compared, nor can private banks or companies be compared. Understanding these central bank characteristics plays a very important role in setting your code of conduct. Since there is only one central bank, you have to be willing to create and abide by the norms on your own, and you often have to make decisions very lonely. We have a duty to set an example to the people at all times and to maintain a high degree of dignity. However, even if there is no object of comparison in Korea, it is also important to be aware that there are many objects of comparison in the world. The central banks of other countries are not the right ones It is the object of doctrine. It can only be seen that the central banks of the United States, Japan, Europe, China, etc ., each of us carry out our duty to the development of the country by acting in such a way that they correspond to their contribution to the development of the global economy, as well as to the country and region . . Now that countries around the world live in a global economy, no economic sector in any country is facing international competition. In the case of the open sector, there is no need to even discuss whether it is internationally competitive, as the sector that is inferior in international competitiveness does not survive in the market . In the end, the international competitiveness of sectors that are not open to the outside world will eventually become the determining factor for the country's national competitiveness. In that sense, it can be said that only when the Bank of Korea is more competitive than other central banks can the Korean economy become more advanced . In this context , if you recognize today that our country's entry into the developed world depends in part on us, your determination will be renewed, and when you work from this perspective, Your future will be bright. You are also motivated to do your work with strength. I would like to emphasize that your views should not remain domestic, and you should always try to maintain an international flair. For new employees, it's going to be hard to get these three messages in your head clearly at once. So I hope you take the time to understand what we're talking about today. In today's very auspicious day, there is only one reason why I would like to say this kind of difficult message to the new employees. The Bank of Korea has many of you seniors who are good and excellent. There is no doubt that if you become better than these predecessors, your future will be bright, and this organization will develop further. If the juniors are less than the seniors, wouldn't it be natural for the organization to regress? I earnestly hope that all of you will become better Qing Chu Nam than your predecessors. If you do a good job of implementing the three things that we have talked about today, of course, I think it will be possible for you to become a hermitage, and for this very purpose I have explained many things at such length. Finally, I hope that you will not forget the grace of your parents and relatives who have dedicated themselves behind the scenes for your day and continue to make the effort to repay them as best they can. Once again , congratulations to all of our new employees! January 2, 2012 Governor Kim Chong-su

I think that when we have sidestories and strategies that fit our reality, we can come up with and take shape. I would like to ask you to lend this position to enhance the capacity of finance itself so that the financial industry can develop by its own creative power. In particular, I think finance needs to work harder on building the capacity of human capital, especially since it is a matter of people after all. Looking back at the lessons of this global financial crisis, the role of financiers is a reminder of the importance of preventing crises. At the root of the financial crisis is a crisis of the real economy, so when a financial crisis occurs, it must be preceded by a careful analysis of the factors of the crisis. And, once a crisis has occurred, there is a tendency to blame the messenger who delivered the crisis without this analysis as the main culprit of the crisis. This is a so-called category of error that stems from a mixture of the perception of imbalances and crises in the economy that the real-financial linkage is functioning properly and the perception of the path of delivery of the crisis ( category mistake). In view of the fact that when finance functions sufficiently to improve the efficiency of the entire economic system that encompasses real and financial, the likelihood of an economic crisis is also minimized, so I would like to emphasize that your role as a financier is significant when it comes to finance , which is ultimately a matter of people. Dear financiers! We look forward to unleashing your skills and skills so that 2012 can be marked as a year of development in our financial history. Let the financiers, the legislators, and the policy authorities all work together to work on the development of finance. On the occasion of a hopeful new year, I wish you and your families a good day of health and happiness all the time. Thanks. January 4, 2012 Han Kuk-eun Hang Gun Kim Su

Attachment 1 Korean Announcement Gist "Will emerging market countries in Asia and Latin America be able to drive the global economic recovery?" (Can Economies from Asia and Latin America be the Drivers of World Recovery?) the topic of the discussion at today's Policy Forum: "Can emerging market countries in Asia and Latin America drive the global economic recovery?" The issue has great implications not only for the recovery of the global economy, but also for the resolution of global imbalances, and we would like to express our views on the subject by answering the following three questions: (1) What is the status and outlook of the Asian and Latin American regions in the world economy? (2) Even if the two regions reduce their dependence on developed countries and switch to an economic structure based on domestic demand, will they still be able to maintain the same dynamic and sustainable growth momentum as they have so far? (3) What are the risk factors that may arise in the transition of the two regions to an economy where growth is driven primarily by domestic demand? (Current position and outlook of the Asian and Latin American economies)  As of 2010, the Asian and Latin American economies* accounted for 37% of global GDP, up 10%p from a decade ago, and according to the IMF, it is expected to rise to 43% in 2017.  "Asia" means 27 countries in the Asian emerging market countries such as China, India, ASEAN, etc., and 31 countries, including the Asian Emerging Industrial Countries (Korea, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Singapore), and "Latin America" means "Latin America" . Refers to the 32 countries along the Latin American continent and the Caribbean In terms of population, the two regions also account for about 3/4 of the population of the three worlds, with the potential to grow into the largest market in the world. Even if you look at the GDP per capita (versus the US) and the middle-class ratio, the purchasing power of both regions, particularly in Asia, has risen rapidly since the 1990s.  In addition, the economies of Asia and Latin America have led the recovery of the global economy by showing rapid growth in the recovery process after the global financial crisis. During the period 2009-2011, the contribution of the two regions to global economic growth reached 56%, and during the same period, Asian emerging market countries demonstrated a high growth rate of 8% at a CAGR. According to the IMF, Asia's contribution to global economic growth is expected to be even higher in the future.  However, in order for the Asian and Latin American economies to continue to play a driving role in global economic growth in the future, we believe that it is necessary to continue to grow by creating new water streams within or between the two regions. Especially given that the downturn in the economies of the developed countries will continue for a considerable period of time, the newly created demand in both regions will have to be quite large and sustainable. (The need to transition to a domestic demand-driven economy)  Since the 2000s, the degree of economic coordination between Asian and Latin American economies and advanced economies has increased*  Correlation of Economic Growth Rates Between Asia-Developed Countries and Latin America-Developed Countries: 0.04 and 0.18 from 1990 to 1999 0.47 and 0.55 in Q3 2000-2008 0.79 and 0.96 in Q4 2008-Q1 2012 The coordination of the trade economy refers to a two-way causal system of growth between emerging market countries and developed countries , but now the causal relationship from developed countries to emerging market countries seems to be larger. In Asia, in particular, the contribution of private consumption to growth and its significantly lower share of GDP are intensifying the phenomenon of economic and growth coordination with developed countries.  The coordination of growth between emerging market countries and developed countries discussed above suggests that the Asian and Latin American economies have great potential to grow as a domestic demand center. However, the task of realizing this potential is not so easy. - In fact, the Asian economy has been making various structural reform efforts since the foreign exchange crisis of the late 1990s to reduce its dependence on the advanced economy, but the results have not been very significant.  Therefore, at this point, it is necessary to examine how much more room there is for Asian and Latin American countries to pursue domestic-driven growth.  First of all, in the short term, Asian and Latin American countries have more room to implement domestic consumption or investment promotion policies than developed countries. In terms of reference interest rates and government debt ratios, there is still room for monetary and fiscal policy, and the macroeconomic fundamentals seen in terms of foreign exchange reserves, inflation, and current balances are also strong. In addition, in the 2000s, the resilience of both regions to negative static shocks in physical or financial terms from abroad also improved significantly. - In fact, it is also due to the fact that the two regional countries have overcome the shock of the global financial crisis or the euro area national debt crisis .  However, as the world economy is expected to return to its pre-crisis growth path and it is expected that it will take a considerable period of time to come for developed countries to regain their fiscal health, emerging market countries are limited in their ability to support global economic growth with expansionary policies alone , and structural reforms are needed as a more fundamental solution. This includes the expansion of the social safety net, the development of financial markets, and the regulatory reform of the product and labor markets.  In addition to the structural reform measures that have been proposed in the past, we would like to emphasize that as an additional measure, domestic demand can also be expanded through the Free Trade Agreement (FTA). In this regard , recent academic studies have shown that the economic growth of emerging market countries is due to the expansion of production of high-value goods or services, rather than to the expansion of trade surplus or export volume itself , and that domestic demand-driven growth can continue as long as the demand for high-value products persists. It is being presented and I think it is necessary to refer to it  FTAs can help meet the domestic demand-oriented growth sustainability requirements of emerging market countries in the following ways: First, the FTA has the effect of promoting consumption because it lowers the import price of goods and services through tariff cuts or the promotion of competition in the domestic market. Second, the FTA has the effect of promoting domestic investment and foreign direct investment by creating new investment opportunities through expanding market size. Third , the FTA could be an opportunity to spark reform and deregulation in areas where competition is limited, especially in areas where competition is limited from abroad, such as the services sector.  In fact, based on the expectation of the growth promoting effect of the FTA, South Korea has signed FTAs with a total of 45 countries (about 60% of the world's GDP), including not only developed but also emerging market countries, and will soon negotiate with China and Japan to conclude FTAs. I plan to start If the ROK, Sino-Japanese FTA is signed, which is currently being pursued, it will become the third largest market in the world after NAFTA and the EU. (Risks and Countermeasures Involved in Changing the Economic Structure)  Meanwhile, emerging market countries in Asia and Latin America are facing the following risks in transitioning to a domestic-oriented growth structure : Asia relies on the world's major reserve currencies for the majority of its international trade and financial settlements, so for macro and financial stability in emerging market countries, unrestricted access to state-owned capital markets is required. In reality, however, there are many uncertainties and constraints in emerging market countries' access to international financial markets, so the reduction of the current account surplus and the reduction of foreign exchange reserves that may occur in the course of these countries' transition to a domestic-driven economy are major risk factors. This risk has been one of the main reasons why emerging market countries have so far not been able to easily transition to a domestic-oriented growth strategy.  Therefore, in order to mitigate these risks, emerging market countries must first minimize the vulnerability of the domestic financial sector and adopt an effective macroprudential framework. The FTA will also help prevent the expansion of external imbalances by simultaneously promoting foreign trade and domestic demand .  However, no less important is the need for developed countries to play an important role in the expansion of the global financial safety net. This is because the major developed countries are likely to be the epicenter of global liquidity instability if global liquidity instability arises as providers of the world's reserve currencies. Attachment 2 Full text of the English presentation Can Economies from Asia and Latin America be the Drivers of World Recovery? Choongsoo Kim Governor, Bank of Korea Asia-LAC High Level Economic Policy Forum Tokyo, Japan, October 13, 2012 Before presenting my views, I would like to thank the Asian Development Bank and the Inter-American Development Bank for inviting me to speak at this conference. I find that the issue for discussion is very topical, and has far reaching implications not only for world economic recovery but also global rebalancing. While the specific questions in the background note are useful to organize our thinking, I will address the issue from a broad perspective by exploring the following three questions:  First, where do Asia and Latin America stand now in the world economy?  Second, can these two regions achieve dynamic and sustainable growth by promoting domestic demand more than they promote exports?  Third, what are the risks that these regions will face as they shift toward domestic demand-driven growth? Where Asia and Latin America stand in the world economy First, let me briefly discuss the question of where Asia and Latin America now stand in the world economy, and how their economic statuses will likely evolve in the future. Asia and Latin America together accounted for 37% of world GDP in 2010, a ten percentage point higher level than they had one decade ago. Extrapolating from current trends, the IMF projects the two regions as likely to account for 43% of world GDP by 2017. And according to a long-term projection by the ADB, meanwhile, Asia alone will account for one-half of global output by 2050. The two regions are also habitats of large populations, close to three-quarters of the worlds total, suggesting their potential to offer the biggest market to the world. And indeed, their purchasing powers, as measured either by their per capita incomes or by the sizes of their middle classes, have risen rapidly since the 1990s, particularly in Asia. What about the contributions of these two regions to world growth? Asia and Latin America have recovered from the global crisis faster than their advanced peers, even if the recoveries have not been uniform across countries within them. Specifically, the two regions accounted for 56% of global growth during 2009-11. Asia's contribution to world growth is expected to become even larger in the years ahead. At first glance all of these figures look quite promising, and one might argue that Asia and Latin America can be the drivers of world economic recovery. For this argument to be realistic, however, there is an important condition that must be met namely, that Asia and Latin America must be able to offer domestic demand for goods and services to the world economy, on a sufficiently large-scale and sustained basis, and independently of advanced economies. Rebalancing sources of growth This consideration naturally leads me to my second question, concerning the prospects for domestic demand-driven growth in these two regions. Asian and Latin American growth performance over the business cycle frequency has become increasingly more synchronized with that of the advanced regions, as can be seen from the rising correlations in growth between the two groups. And the synchronization has become even tighter after the global crisis. While this evidence should in principle reflect two-way causality, the causality, at the moment, seems to be running more strongly from the advanced regions to Asia and Latin America than the other way around. Moreover, for emerging Asia, private consumption accounts for a far smaller share of GDP than in the advanced regions or Latin America, and its contribution to growth is also significantly smaller. Two broad implications are borne out from these features of Asia and Latin America. First, there is room for promoting domestic demand-driven growth especially in Asia, while Latin America has good potential to grow further with more investment and international trade. Second, it may nevertheless not be easy to promote domestic demand on a sustained basis, particularly in Asia. This latter implication may not be obvious at first glance, but the truth is that Asia has been less successful in decoupling itself from the advanced regions since the Asian crisis, even despite various reform efforts to this end. I think now is the opportune time for Asia and Latin America to rethink about their growth strategies. If we focus on the short-run, both regions do appear to have greater policy spaces than their advanced peers for boosting domestic demand consumption in Asia and investment for Latin Americagiven their sound macro fundamentals and improved resilience to financial shocks of external origin. In this setting, further fiscal and monetary stimulus should help to boost domestic demand and, ultimately, world recovery. However, fiscal and monetary stimulus cannot be a durable solution to world recovery. Many predict that it will take years, if not a full decade, for the world economy to return to growth on par with its pre-crisis trends and for advanced economies to restore fiscal soundness. Thus, if Asia and Latin America are to lead world recovery for years to come, they should look beyond the short-run policy stimulus. This is why structural reforms are called for, to enhance productivity growth. Many studies have identified a long list of reforms that could enhance growth and help reduce the dependence on external demand. For example, better social safety nets could help to reduce precautionary savings, while domestic financial development could support more efficient resource alloc ation and better risk hedging. Product and labor market deregulations would also contribute to increased productivity by eliminating distortions. I will not go into detail regarding such reforms, as they have already been discussed extensively. What I would instead like to speculate on now is another policy option that can be added, to the existing list of reforms for Asia and Latin America. It is Free Trade Agreements, or FTAs in short. I know it may sound odd to speak of FTAs as structural means for boosting domestic demand. But let me elaborate. A recent study has convincingly argued that it is the production of high value-added goods and services rather than trade surpluses or exports, what characterizes growth in emerging economies, and that domestic demand-driven growth could materialize on a sustained basis provided the demand for such goods and services is maintained. I think FTAs could help emerging economies to meet the stated condition of this argument. To be specific, FTAs can bolster domestic consumption by making foreign goods and services more affordable at home at cheaper prices and by attracting more foreign direct investment. FTAs could also act as triggers for needed reforms and deregulation, particularly in the service sector where foreign competition has typically been limited. Risks down the road What risks would Asia and Latin America face if they were to depart from their long-cherished growth strategies? Both regions are highly dollarized in their international trade and finance and, for Latin America, also in domestic finance. As such, free and unfettered access to the international capital markets is a key to macro and financial stability in both regions. But the reality is uncertain and often limited market access. And shifting toward more domestic demand-driven growth may lead to stronger home currencies and smaller foreign exchange buffers than at present. Concerns about such risks may have in fact discouraged or delayed the desired economic transitions in many Asian and Latin American countries until now. Both regions need to protect themselves from such financial risks by minimizing their financial vulnerabilities at home and developing effective macro-prudential frameworks. But I should stress here that advanced countries can and should also play a role in strengthening the global financial safety nets. Their role in this regard is essential, because they supply the reserve currencies and, therefore by construction, they are most likely to be the sources of any global liquidity disruptions that might occur in the future. Conclusion So in conclusion, my answer to the question posed for this session, "Can the Economies from Asia and Latin America be the Drivers of World Recovery?" is yes, they can  conditional on better and more proactive global cooperation in finance and trade. I hope that my optimistic view proves correct, for the benefit of us all. Thank you for your attention. 3 Forum Program Asia-LAC High Level Economic Policy Forum Asia-Latin America: New Engines of Growth of the Global Economy? text: 2013 Pan-Financial Institution New Year's Society 2013 Pan-Financial Institution New Year's Society god year Four god year Four 2013. 1. 3 Number of total re-imitations to the ROK Dear financiers! Today, the city that plays a pivotal role in the financial industry in our country is very happy to be able to share New Year's greetings with you. In the new year, as our financial community makes a significant contribution to the recovery of the real economy, I sincerely wish you all the best in doing as a financier. Over the past year, uncertainty has persisted throughout the year regarding the euro area fiscal crisis, the fiscal and monetary policies of major countries, and the political calendar at home and abroad. In particular, the protracted economic crisis in the euro area has greatly weakened the recovery of developed economies, and the impact has also significantly slowed the growth of emerging market borders. The ROK economy has also experienced a significant decline in growth rates above its potential level due to the sluggish growth rate of exports and domestic demand due to the global slowdown and the psychological contraction of economic actors. This year, as uncertainty eases somewhat, our economy will show a modest improvement trend, but the pace of recovery in growth is slow, and the negative GDP gap in which the actual gross domestic product (GDP) of the country is below the potential level is expected to continue. Financial markets remain largely stable, with the potential for increased volatility in capital oil flows and price variables as a result of the unfolding of the euro area fiscal crisis, quantitative easing in major developed countries and changes in the way monetary policy is operated. Dear financiers! In the future, I believe that the role of not only the policy authorities but also the financiers is important for our economy to increase its resilience to domestic and international shocks and to move away from low growth. First, financial institutions should intensify their efforts to diversify their revenue streams, such as improving management efficiency and opening up new markets in response to the fact that the operating environment has changed significantly from the past , such as the reduction of interest margins due to the impact of low interest rates . In addition, financial institutions should faithfully perform their original mission, the function of financial intermediary, and join in supporting the recovery of the growth rate of our economy. As long as the financial intermediary function is not functioning properly, it is difficult for the actual water economy to be vibrant. The Bank of Korea intends to establish a total cap loan support sector so that support for high-use and growth-contributing sectors can be strengthened in the future. Financial institutions should also redouble their efforts to actively identify and support companies with great growth potential. In addition, as the economic slowdown continues, it is inevitable that marginal companies will be restructured, but the selectivity of loans to financial institutions should be increased so that even superior SMEs are not bankrupted due to a temporary lack of liquidity. We should also be mindful of expanding financial inclusion for the financial underprivileged. In the meantime, the formation of financial institutions in accordance with financial autonomy  In the process of globalization, as competition between financial institutions intensified, the focus was on commerce and not neglecting the public. It is necessary to look back. We must continue our efforts to expand the financial interests of the common people and provide appropriate financial services to the financial underprivileged. The Bank of Korea will do its best to ensure that your efforts as financiers bear fruit. Title: Celebration of the 16th Seoul International Financial Forum
text: Financial News "16th Seoul International Financial Forum" Barn 2015. 4. 22. Bank of Korea Governor Lee Lee Yeol President Jeon Jae-ho Financial News, and all the guests and professionals at home and abroad! First of all, I am very pleased to congratulate you at the Seoul International Finance Forum for the sixteenth time this year. The Seoul International Finance Forum has brought together the best experts at home and abroad every year to suggest the direction in which Korean finance will move forward in the midst of the great current of the global economy. In particular, the forum is based on the theme of fintech, which has recently emerged as a hot topic of financial innovation at home and abroad , and is expected to once again serve as a guide to the development of the domestic financial industry. As you well know, fintech is a new term that refers to the convergence of finance and technology. But the concept itself is not new. Already since the mid-1990s, the development of information and communication technology (IT) has brought about revolutionary changes in the doors of the Ministry of Finance, which has sparked a vigorous discussion on "electronic money", "IT companies entering the financial industry", and "de-intermediary of finance ". At that time, electronic money had already emerged in the United States and Europe, and specialized banks on the Internet had been established. Now, more than 20 years later, the combination of finance and IT has been reborn at home and abroad under the name of 'fintech' and is rapidly affecting our real lives. This is above all because the proliferation of smartphones has made it possible to conduct financial transactions regardless of time and place, and when big data analysis is able to provide financial services that meet the characteristics and needs of high-end customers, it is the door when fintech has laid the foundation for the development of the industry into an industry . I think. It's as if the computer was first invented in 1946, but it took more than 30 years to popularize it as a personal computer (PC). Until now, traditional financial institutions have leveraged IT to expand the field of financial services , but now ordinary companies are challenging the realm of financial institutions through IT. Global IT companies such as Google, Apple, and Alibaba are expanding their work area to include micropayments based on the Internet and social media, as well as services that directly connect financial consumers and providers. In addition, in underdeveloped countries such as Africa, South America, and Asia, we provide gold financing services to the financial underprivileged through IT-based storeless banking instead of bank stores. As such, fintech is not only becoming a new trend in the financial industry around the world, but it is also widely used as a means of financial inclusion. Ladies and gentlemen! There is also a growing expectation that fintech innovation , which is currently spreading rapidly at home and abroad, will play a breakthrough role in overcoming the global financial industry downturn that has persisted since the global financial crisis. In the aftermath of the financial crisis, when growth has stagnated and the continuation of low interest rates has made it difficult to increase profits through financial intermediaries, fintech is believed to be a new monetization model for the gold financing industry and to develop into a new growth engine industry. On the one hand, we should also look at whether there are any challenges that we have to solve with regard to the proliferation of fintech. In the short term, we will continue to push for the reorganization of the regulatory system necessary to cultivate the Pintek industry without fail, and we must also make every effort to ensure the security and safety of fintech services. In the longer run, we should also look at whether the impact of innovation is likely to cause unexpected side effects as the industry grows rapidly. Expectations of the emergence of a "new economy" following the IT revolution in the late 1990s led to the collapse of the dot-com bubble a few years later, and the proliferation of derivatives based on the development of "financial engineering" in the mid-2000s led to the emergence of U.S. subprime mortgages. It is important to note that it was also the main cause of the eventuality. Dear Distinguished Guests, at home and abroad! Fintech is now a key element of financial innovation. Major global banks are already expanding their investments by recognizing the importance of the fintech industry , and in developed financial countries such as the UK, competition between countries for market preemption is intensifying, with governments stepping up to nurture the fintech industry. Under such circumstances, it is very encouraging that at the beginning of this year, our government decided to actively cultivate the fintech industry by establishing a "plan to support IT and financial convergence." The Bank of Korea will also support the development of the fintech industry by monitoring fintech-related leasing factors and formulating measures to ensure the safety of new payment services. If the world-class IT infrastructure that our country possesses is combined with the creativity of the private sector and the support of government authorities , I am confident that the future of the domestic fintech industry will be bright. In any case, we look forward to a variety of in-depth discussions at this forum that can serve as a basis for the future development of the fintech industry in our country. Once again, we would like to congratulate you on holding the Seoul International Financial Forum. Thanks.
