Title: All remarks of Commissioner Ko Seung-beom "Press Conference Organized by the Gold Barrel Committee"
text: Financial and Monetary Commission Press Conference Materials Financial and Monetary Commission Press Conference Materials 2019. 7. 3 Financial and Monetary Commissioner Ko Seung Bum * This document is not an official opinion of the Bank of Korea or the Financial and Monetary Commission, but the personal opinion of the Gold Barrel Commissioner.  foreword It's nice to have the opportunity again after 1 year of press conference in July last year. We emphasized the importance of financial stability at the time, and a lot has changed in 1 year. In the second half of last year, the issue of financial stability was highlighted, and this year, the issue of economic and price control is becoming more prominent. In the past year, I have emphasized the importance of financial stability and briefly mentioned my thoughts on the relationship between economic growth, financial development, and financial stability, and I would like to tell you more about this. First of all, let me briefly summarize what I said last year. There have been a variety of theoretical and empirical studies that suggest that financial development has a positive impact on economic growth. In theory, various opinions have been proposed, including the view that financial development affects the parameters of technological development in the function of production 1)2), the number of material deficits 3)4) or the level of human capital 5). Empirical analysis was also followed to verify the theoretical analysis. In particular, using the method of Ship (1991)6), King and Levine (1993)7) analyzed it based on cross-sectional data from 80 countries created using data from 1960 to 1989 , and the development of finance in the same bunseok As a proxy variable, we used indicators such as the 'Total Liquid Debt/GDP Ratio of the Financial Sector'. Their analysis showed that financial development had a positive impact on economic growth. However, if we define financial development as the ratio of total liquid debt to GDP or the ratio of private debt to GDP, contrary to the general conclusion, it has also been argued that in Latin American countries, financial development in the early days of economic growth has had an inverted negative effect on economic growth. 8) In the early '80s, Mexico, and many other countries experienced financial crises following policies of rapid financial liberalization. Through the opening up of the financial markets, a large amount of foreign capital was introduced, and the outflow of foreign capital due to the increase in interest rates in the United States led to the financial crisis. In the process of opening up the financial markets, it was believed that financial development was achieved by the rapidly increasing credit, that is, the increase in liquidity in the financial sector, but economic growth fell sharply. 9) In other words, financial development, defined as liquidity, was rather negative for growth in the early stages of economic growth.  Financial Development and Economic Growth In the last 10 years, studies have been conducted that highlight the side effects of excessive financial development. Financial development plays a positive role in the growth of the economy, but if the development of the financial sector goes beyond a certain extent, it will have a negative impact on the economy. According to them, not only in the early stages of economic development, but also in developed countries where the economy has reached the stage of maturity, excessive financial development is negative for the economy, and they have mostly considered the increase in private credit as a proxy variable for the financial start-up. One of the studies in this regard is Chekhetti and Karubi (2012)10). Their research concluded that financial development, as measured by the ratio of private credit, has a positive and positive effect on economic growth up to a certain threshold , but a negative impact after that threshold. In other words, a "reverse U-shaped parabola" relationship is established between financial development and economic growth , and the private credit ratio of 100% to GDP is claimed to be the critical point. The same is true when the private credit ratio of the banking sector was used instead of the total private credit ratio, and after a certain threshold we found a negative impact, with a 90% ratio of private credit to GDP being at a critical point. As such, research using the private credit ratio continued, and according to Hwang Soon-ju (2017)11), the ratio of private credit to GDP of 88-100% is suggested in various studies as a threshold for financial development to have an inadvertent effect on economic growth. There have also been studies that divide the total credit in the economy into governments, corporations, and household segments, and that if they cross a certain threshold, they will have a negative impact on economic growth , and that excessive increases in household sector leverage could lead to a financial crisis . . First, Chekhetti and Zampoli (2011)12) used data from 18 OECD countries between 1980 and 2010 to quantify that if the size of credit to GDP in an economy exceeds a certain threshold, it will have a negative impact on economic growth. Bo Yeo-jun Bar. According to them, the thresholds were 85% for government sector credit, 90% for corporate credit, and 85% for household credit, respectively. Their conclusion is that "excessive debt is detrimental to growth." High debt is bad for growth.) It was. As a result of this study, the World Economic Forum (WEF) in its 2010 report13 set a threshold of 75% of household credit, 80% of corporate credit, and 90% of government sector credit as the percentage of GDP. The IMF analyzed in its 2017 Global Financial Stability Report (GFSR)14 that household debt increases the likelihood of a silver act. According to the IMF, household debt is As it increases, the probability of a bank crisis also increases , especially if the household debt/GDP ratio ratio is above 65%, which greatly increases the probability of a bank crisis. What these studies have in common is that excessive increases in household debt can be a negative factor for economic growth, and by increasing the likelihood of a banking crisis, they are not even good in terms of financial stability. The sum of non-financial sector debts such as governments, corporations, households, etc. is sometimes called macro leverage , and in the case of Korea, the macro leverage ratio to GDP is 230%, as private credit is close to 200%, despite the fact that the government-sector debt is lower than in other countries. Beyond that. Which sector of macro leverage is particularly problematic varies from country to country. In our case, household debt is perceived as a problem, but China has high corporate debt as a problem, and many of the countries in Ruff have had problems with government bonds.  Financial Development and Financial Stability Contrary to the expectation that financial development will have a positive impact on economic growth , many economic researchers have shown through empirical analysis that what we consider to be financial development may be negative for economic growth. There are many studies that show that gold financing, defined as the expansion of the private credit supply, has a negative impact not only on economic growth but also on financial stability if it exceeds a certain level. Since the '90s, and especially in the 2000s, with the emergence of many derivatives using financial engineering techniques , it was believed that these financial innovations would advance finance through functions such as risk differentiation and stimulate economic growth. However, these financial innovations, as are well known, were also the cause of the 2008 global financial crisis. One thing to be said here is that the financial instability that led to the global financial crisis is not solely due to the development of financial engineering. Another important cause of financial instability was the oversupplied size of credit under the mitigating financial conditions leading up to the mid-2000s . This was also attributed to financial development, but the excessive supply of credit eventually had a negative impact on economic growth. Under the influence of the collapse of the U.S. dot-com bubble in the early 2000s , the Fed has been on a low-interest rate trajectory. However, this low-interest rate policy led to the expansion of credit, and in the process of providing credit to gold lenders in a (9) controversy , lending standards were also greatly loosened. This increase in credit was injected into the housing market and other self-produced markets, which created a boom in the housing market and the stock market in the mid-2000s. 15) Taylor(200) 7)16) argued that if the U.S. Fed had followed the Taylor Rule in 2002-06 and brought the policy rate higher, there would have been no large-scale spread of the housing bubble and its collapse. In response to these allegations, however, former Fed Chairman Bernanke has denied any link between monetary policy and house prices.  Accumulation of financial imbalances Meanwhile , in the course of overcoming the 2008 global financial crisis, the easing monetary policy of the major countries has had the effect of preventing (9) a sharp contraction in the country. Traditional and non-traditional monetary policies, such as rate cuts and quantitative easing to overcome the crisis, have succeeded in preventing (9) from deteriorating sharply to the level of "The Great Depression" period, resulting in the period following the global financial crisis being followed by the Great Depression. It's called the contrasting "The Great Recession." However, in the course of thus avoiding the (9) period of the steep cooling, the problem of financial imbalances caused by increased leverage has arisen, and in the process of overcoming the crisis triggered by the expansion of credit, again the problem of increasing leverage has arisen. It has emerged. Noting that monetary policy is closely linked to the process by which the expansion of credit leads to the accumulation of financial imbalances, it has been argued that monetary policy formulation needs to be taken into account when formulating monetary policy, mainly by the Bank for International Settlements (BIS). Borio (2012)17, the head of the BIS Monetary (9) Empire, emphasized the importance of the financial cycle and emphasized that in order to fully consider it, monetary policy , fiscal policy, and macroprudential policies need to be looked at from a medium-term clock. . The vulnerability of the financial sector accumulates over a long period of time , and it also takes a long time to deal with it. In other words, the short-term view of market participants and policy officials makes a significant contribution to the creation of a financial crisis. In a paper published the following year (2013)18 with other colleagues at BIS, Borio also emphasized the importance of the financial cycle, noting that measuring the potential growth rate and output gap taking into account the financial cycle is Insisted on being important. They strongly insist on the need for a financially neutral output gap measurement, and even if inflation is stable, when financial imbalances are accumulated, (9) I argued that I could deviate from potential growth (9). This discussion of the BIS has evolved from the discussion of the financially neutral output gap, which has also led to the study of estimating the financial neutral mid-term interest rate. According to Celius and Borio et al. (2016)19), if we estimate it taking into account the financial cycle, the potential growth rate will be lower than (9)woo of the estimate by the general model, and therefore the output gap will be a smaller negative width or even a slight plus. Insisted. And it was argued that the (9) right of the neutral rate would be higher than the (9) right of the general estimate. According to them, the easing monetary policy of the major countries at the time was actually more relaxed than expected. "Responding after financial stability risks have become current is to respond too little, and too late, which results in ignoring the cumulative impact of policies in the entire financial cycle," they said. Insisted. In a speech in November 2018, Borio said that the monetary policy system is entirely dependent on "faith " and that the role of price stability and financial stability is important in accumulating faith so that it can operate well. "Price stability and financial stability are inextricably linked, but in reality, the two are more like an inconvenient relationship than a perfect part." This is contrary to the general view of Adrian and Shin Hyun-song (2009)21) that "monetary and financial stability policies should be viewed separately, and the two policies are inseparable. At the very least, both policies should be done in close cooperation for a long time."  Warning about excessive credit If we look back at past history, we can see that many of the financial crises that the world has been through over the years have been triggered by credit confirmations. There is a lot of research on financial crises, but among them, Kindleberger's work is considered the most important in the history of financial crises, and the work of Reinhart and Rogoff, published after the 2008 global financial crisis , is also a very extensive study. Kindleberger and Aliber wrote in his book Madness, Panic, Collapse  The History of Financial Crisis [22] that since the tulip bubble in the Netherlands in 1636, the Nasdaq stock market bubble in the United States in 1995-2000 The top 10 financial bubbles are described so far. 23) The hallmark of the top 10 bubbles is that most of them have been in the real estate market or the stock market since this credit expansion. The authors, who argue that bubbles are always supposed to burst, emphasize that "the cycle of madness and panic is due to fluctuations in the supply of credit going up and down with (9) a cyclical wave." They analyzed the phase correlation of different bubbles, especially those that have appeared over the course of about 15 years since the mid-80s . According to them, the Japanese stock market and real estate bubble in the late '80s, the East Asian foreign exchange crisis of '97, and the dot-com bubble in the United States in the early 2000s are closely related. In other words, after the collapse of the Japanese bubble, the funds released were brought into Southeast Asian countries such as Thailand, Indonesia and Malaysia, and the real estate and securities prices of these Asian countries collapsed and then went through the Asian foreign exchange crisis. Since then, the money that has fled East Asia has flowed into the United States, which is claimed to have led to the dot-com bubble in the United States in the late '90s and early 2000s. As Kindleberger pointed out that "the financial crisis is like a hardy perennials that keeps blooming," in the end, excessive credit has moved around and created a crisis. They also criticized the central bank's role in the financial crisis, saying, "The heads of central banks will not traditionally avoid raising rates in order to prevent inflation from rising. On the other hand, they are extremely reluctant to attempt to cope with the asset price bubble. Even if the existence of bubbles seems to be recognized on the basis of facts, they are not willing to acknowledge the existence of bubbles or even the possibility that they existed in the past." Title: Inaugural Address of Bank of Korea Governor Lee Sung-tae
text: Resignation 2006. 4. 3. President of bank of Korea Lee Sung-tae Dear Bank of Korea Employees! Today, I am here to be appointed Governor of the Bank of Korea , an important pillar of our country's economic policy. I am deeply grateful for the support of my seniors, colleagues, and employees who have been with me to this day. It is a great honor personally to be the head of a central bank that I have been in for a lifetime, and I cannot forbid the daunting imprisonment. On the other hand, it is also reducing the importance of the task of hastening the leap to the advanced economy. First of all, I would like to take this opportunity to express my sincere gratitude to the former Governor Park Seung, who has led the Bank of Korea with excellent insight and high virtue for the past 4 years. Ms. Park has greatly increased the independence and stature of the party and has made great achievements in the advancement of monetary policy. I hope that you will always be healthy in the future , and I ask you to continue to advise me on the development of the party. Dear Bank of Korea Family! Since the second half of last year, our economy has seen a steady increase in exports and a solid recovery centered on domestic and private consumption. From now on, we must make policy efforts to build a foundation for a sustainable stability zone as we consolidate this upward trend. However, it is true that there are also not many challenges to be overcome. We are concerned that the link between economic growth and investment will weaken, and that the growth potential will be reduced by aging and low birth rates. With the progress of liberalization prominently polarizing between industrial sectors , the employment absorption capacity of growth is also declining overall. In the manufacturing sector, which has enjoyed a comparative advantage so far, the pursuit of late-developing countries is accelerating , while the competitiveness of new technologies and service industries is still far behind that of developed countries. These difficulties are largely due to the structural factors that arise as our economy transitions to maturity and the rapid changes in the global economic environment, such as liberalization, intellectualization, and the rise of low-wage economies. Therefore, economic management or corporate management methods based on regulation and protection can no longer be used. In such a situation, the future of our economy depends on how we can secure efficiency and competitiveness at the global level at an early stage. To this end, what is most important is to further strengthen the market functions throughout the economic management system to drive creative innovation efforts by the private sector. For vulnerable sectors, effective support measures should be provided for the cultivation of spontaneity or structural transformation. We should also take a more proactive stance in the flow of openness, such as the expansion of FTA conclusions, and use it as an occasion to promote the reorganization of the industrial structure. In order for these structural reform efforts to achieve the desired results, it is necessary to continue steadily in the long run, and this will only be possible if the stability of the economy is supported. In this regard, the role of the central bank, which is responsible for price stability and financial stability , is more important than ever. Dear Employees! Now I would like to tell you about what you need to keep in mind when it comes to managing monetary policy in the future. We need to maintain policy consistency to increase the predictability of the market. To operate monetary policy consistently, you need to have an eye for the medium- to long-term flow of the economy. Therefore, it is necessary to further strengthen the research and research function and focus our core competencies on the analysis of the economic situation and the economic outlook. The timeliness of the policy should also not be neglected. In recent years, as the economic structure and behavior of economic actors have changed dramatically, and the causal relationship between economic variables has become uncertain, it has become increasingly difficult to accurately predict future economic conditions . This uncertainty forces central banks to be cautious in their policy decisions, but that doesn't mean they shouldn't be put into practice. In some cases, you need to be able to make bold decisions, even at the risk of uncertainty. Communication with the financial markets should also be smoother. Financial markets are the most important partner of the central bank as it is the primary ripple route of monetary policy. We must enhance the policy effect and increase transparency by conveying the policy intent of the party as an appropriate signal to the financial market and reinforcing the feedback channels that converge on the expectations and reactions of market participants. Dear Bank of Korea Family! The real foundation of the central bank's existence is the trust of the people. The trust of the people is only gained when we fulfill our duties and the achievements are accumulated. From this point of view, the emphasis on the operation of the organization should be placed on the expansion of the party's capacity as a policy institution. As the work of the party requires a high degree of expertise in any field, it is necessary to actively train professional personnel and firmly establish a competency-oriented personnel management system. The organizational system will also have to be re-examined to see if there is no room for improvement in terms of synergies. Furthermore, we must immediately embark on the task of envisioning, refining, and refining the medium- and long-term strategy so that we can anticipate and respond to the changes in the future role of the party. We would like to urge you to make your own development efforts. Central banks are in a monopoly position in terms of business, and because competitors are not immediately in front of their eyes, they are prone to self-righteousness or indolence. But other domestic policy institutions as well as foreign central banks are invisible competitors. We should all devote ourselves more fully to self-development so that we can become the best experts in our respective fields of work. In addition, when we do our jobs, we need to establish practices that lead to the best possible conclusions through the joint research and active participation of many employees in discussions. Our role as an objective evaluator and policy advisor to the macroeconomy must also continue to expand. As the public's interest in economic issues increases, there are growing voices calling for a neutral central bank's opinion on major financial and economic issues and for rational alternatives. In order to meet these expectations, we must actively exchange opinions with experts from relevant institutions, including the government, in a more active and open manner to broaden the scope of understanding and empathy. Dear Employees! Now, with a new commitment, let us all gather our strength and wisdom to make the Bank of Korea a state institution that is restrained in autonomy and united in a well-intentioned competition so that the best experts can work most dynamically. Thanks.

New Year's resignation in 2007 Lee Sung-tae , President of Bank of Korea Dear Bank of Korea Family! Today is the day to start the New Year's work with new aspirations and determination . First of all , I would like to extend my gratitude to all the employees who have faithfully performed their duties in the past year. In retrospect, the path our economy has taken in the past year has never been smooth. The pressure to raise the yuan continued, international oil prices rose dramatically , and North Korea's push for nuclear tests increased the risk of geopolitical stability. On the one hand, the lack of employment growth and deteriorating trade conditions have raised concerns about soaring house prices and the consequent leakage of household debt as the economy continues to decline. Even in these difficult conditions, it is estimated that the annual GDP growth rate has reached the 5% mark as the domestic economy continues its upward trajectory driven by strong exports and a steady increase in domestic demand. Water prices had the lowest rate of rise since 2001, and the current resin maintained a black tide. In view of this economic situation, the monetary policy of the year was operated in the direction of gradually reducing the degree of financial completion in line with the trend of improvement of the real economy, paying attention to the price plan. The call rate target was raised by 0.25 percentage points each on three occasions in February, June and August, adjusting it to 4.5% per annum. After September, we kept the call rate table intact in the sense that it was necessary to watch the trend of the economic woes at home and abroad, which has heightened the uncertainty. In November and December, we increased the reserve rate for KRW and foreign currency deposits in order to curb the rapid expansion of credit to financial institutions by foreign borrowing funds, etc., to enhance the effectiveness of interest rate policies. In addition, the total loan limit for the first quarter of 2007 was significantly reduced in view of the trend of improving financial funds use conditions in the small and medium-sized enterprises. Han Eun Family! This year's economic growth rate will be slightly lower than last year's, at around 4.4%, but the pace of growth is expected to gradually increase as we move into the second half of the year. Prices will increase the rise in service charges, but the demand pressure is not great, and the supply and demand of international raw materials, including crude oil, will also increase. It is expected to remain stable as it appears to be smooth. The current water supply is likely to be largely balanced by the widening deficit in the service balance, despite a solid increase in exports. As such, it is expected that in the new year, our economy will not have much difficulty unless the conditions abroad deteriorate significantly. However, from a medium- to long-term perspective, we are facing structural problems that have led to a contraction in investment activity and a trending decline in growth potential. Therefore, in the operation of economic policy, the emphasis should be placed on expanding the foundation for sustainable growth in the long run, rather than considering short-term changes in the situation . In terms of macro-policy, uncertainty should be reduced by settling the price stabilization mechanism and minimizing the amplitude of the economic change. In the microscopic sense, we must revive the motivation to invest by establishing a system in which the creativity of the private sector can lead to efficiency through market competition by drastically overhauling unnecessary regulations. In addition, we should actively pursue measures to strengthen the principle of competition in the service industry and other comparative station gates through market opening. In addition, we must hasten to discover and nurture the next generation of growth engine industry that follows the IT industry. Han Eun Family! Now, let me tell you about the main tasks that the Bank of Korea will be pursuing this year with an emphasis on it. Starting this year, a new medium-term price stabilization target will be in place. As the performance of the first year can have a huge impact on the entire goal-setting period, in the new year, we should strive more than ever to solidify the foundation for price stability. In addition, as the target indicator has shifted from source inflation to consumer prices that are more sensitive to external shocks, more careful attention will need to be paid to identifying the underlying movements of prices. The interest rate policy is a policy that will operate flexibly so that the trend of improvement of the real economy can continue while maintaining price stability. In addition, as an information variable for the determination of medium-term price risk, we will check the trends of monetary indicators and strengthen monitoring of the money supply path and asset market. We should do more to improve the effectiveness of the policy. To this end, by expanding the feedback channels with financial markets and by further elaborating the time signaling, the predictability of the policy and the two You're going to have to build your reputation. Nor should we neglect to strengthen our capacity to forecast the economy and analyze policy effects to ensure market confidence in policy consistency and timeliness. The operation of monetary policy instruments must also be continuously improved. In order to make the interest rate path work more smoothly, it will be necessary to establish a linkage operating system for the long-term operation and the loan and support system when disclosed. At the same time, it is necessary to explore ways to alleviate the leakage pressure of monetary stability securities, while also examining ways to reduce the limit for each financial institution in the medium to long term and to operate mainly on one degree per regional headquarters. Financial stability efforts should be further intensified. In the meantime, as the size of household debt has increased significantly, mainly in the form of state mortgages, and the stability of the financial market has become weaker, it is necessary to seek a system of checks on this and to act quickly if signs of insecurity are detected. In addition, in view of the possibility of increasing the settlement risk due to the expansion of non-bank financial institutions' participation in the payment system, we should strengthen the monitoring of the payment system and earnestly promote the project of building the next-generation mixed payment system. We should pay more attention to the efficient operation of foreign currency assets. In addition to strengthening the comprehensive management system of assets and liabilities, we must continuously improve our investment techniques, risk management and performance appraisal system. At the same time, as we see the effects of the measures to expand currency swap trading, there should be a more forward-looking review of the issue of the utilization of foreign exchange reserves. A new banknote should also be issued without a hitch. Following the issuance of a new five thousand won right in January last year, we plan to issue a new full and one thousand won right from January 22 of this year. In order to ensure that the people do not experience the slightest inconvenience, we will work closely with the relevant pipes including financial institutions to formulate new banknotes. You'll have to be prepared for that. National economic education should also be further internalized. In order to cultivate a rational economic consciousness for young people and young people , and to benefit the general public from the actual economic life, we should differentiate between educational media and content, and use this as an opportunity to broaden our understanding of the central bank. Han Eun Family! The Bank of Korea is now undergoing a period of great transformation. If any organization changes on its own and fails to adapt to a different environment, it will eventually lose its foundation. Central banks are no exception. The accelerated evolution of financial markets, the upgrading of the structure of the economy and the increasing uncertainty raise the need for us to continue to expand our policy capabilities. And increased independence demands greater accountability and publicity. The "Medium- and Long-Term Development Strategy" announced last year was a tie-in to all of our willingness to self-innovate in order to adapt to these changes in the environment. Some of these measures are already being implemented , but we will have to pursue them in earnest this year. In line with the changes in the number of jobs and the work of the Munger, we should prepare a medium- and long-term organizational expenses and personnel relocation plan in the direction of strengthening the ability of the company and the training and lightweighting the internal management sector. And firmly establish a personnel management system based on achievements and abilities, and The remuneration system will also have to be reorganized from the existing soft supply type to the focus on job values and performance. Please keep in mind that this self-innovation is a necessary choice in order to further consolidate the foundation of the company's development, and that the momentum comes from the fact that you employees come together and actively participate. As long as we all make a concerted effort with one heart, our bank will soon become a central bank that is more trusted by the people. Dear Han family ! This year, let us do our best to do our job with the sense of calling of the central banker to lead the development of our economy. As we welcome the New Year , may you and your families be filled with health and happiness. Thanks.
