Title: 56th Anniversary Celebration
text: Commemorative speech for the 56th anniversary of its founding 2006. 6. 12 Bank of Korea President Lee Sung-tae Dear Bank of Korea Family! Today marks fifty-six stones since the Bank of Korea was founded as the central bank of the country. First of all, I would like to express my sincere gratitude to the many people who have lent this position and have given encouragement and guidance to the establishment of a national bank today. In addition, I would like to congratulate you for the hard work of our employees who are faithfully performing their duties. The ROK economy is showing a solid recovery since the second half of last year, with domestic demand surviving mainly on private consumption, while exports have maintained a high growth trend. In response to this trend of improvement in the real economy, the party has raised its call rate target on four occasions in order to maximize the side effects of the continuation of the low interest rate trend and to proactively cope with the expected inflationary pressures in the future. The current policy rate is still considered to be sufficient to support the economic uptick in light of the overall financial and economic situation. Dear Bank of Korea Family! In recent years, as overseas conditions have become worse than expected, concerns have been raised about whether the upward trend in the domestic economy can continue. Falling exchange rates are seen as a slowdown in exports and a decline in corporate mining, while rising international oil prices can shrink private sector costs through deteriorating trade conditions. However, if the exchange rate or oil price situation does not deteriorate significantly than at present, our economy is expected to continue its upward phase in the second half of the year with a steady increase in exports and domestic demand. The growth rate will be somewhat modest, but this is partly due to the underlying effect of the high growth rate. And the current water supply, which has recorded a 3-month annual deficit since last February, is also likely to return to the black tide. Meanwhile, prices remain stable overall, but the upward pressure is likely to gradually increase as the economy recovers and oil prices continue , and we must continue to watch the movement of real estate prices. Dear Bank of Korea Family! Due to the rapid changes in domestic and international conditions, the environment for the operation of monetary policy is also changing significantly. Above all, the phenomenon of global low water prices, which began to appear in the 2000s, is gradually taking hold. This calls on us to renew our awareness of price stability. Approaching the issue of price stability from a conventional perspective may lead to an oversupply of fluid dynamics. As part of the party's inaugural celebration, the holding of the Zero International Conference on "Monetary Policy Under Low Inflation" is also part of an effort to explore a new policy paradigm. Advances in liberalization and globalization are also presenting us with another challenge. As capital trading expands at a faster pace than light commerce, volatility is also growing as the phenomenon of international coordination of price variables, such as interest rate exchange rate and stock prices, becomes prominent. Accordingly, there is great independence in the operation of monetary policy. While being constrained , there is an increased need to consider foreign factors more closely. As the financial economic structure became complex and multi-flagged, the behavior of economic coefficients changed dramatically. In the wake of the foreign exchange crisis, the risk-averse tendency in corporate management has become stronger, and the consumption pattern of households is showing a different pattern from the past , such as the increase in the proportion of services and overseas consumption. In the financial markets, a large flow of financial institution goddesses In the midst of the transition from the corporate to the household sector, the trading of new financial products such as derivatives has increased significantly, and the phenomenon of market expectations is also frequent. As a result, the traditional causal system between economic variables has weakened, and the ripple path and effects of monetary policy have become equally uncertain. In order to ensure the adequacy and effectiveness of monetary policy under these different conditions, it is necessary to be able to more accurately diagnose and predict the flow of economic and financial affairs at home and abroad. On that basis, we will also need to increase our ability to examine market expectations and gauge the expected response, thus continuously increasing the real-world suitability of monetary policy. Dear Bank of Korea Family! Now, let me tell you about the issues that the Bank of Korea should focus on and pursue after the second half of the year. First of all , the interest rate policy should continue to operate in the direction of responding proactively to inflationary pressures while keeping an eye on economic trends. In addition, the new price stability targets, which will be in effect from next year, are preferable to be set early, given the ripple lag in policy, etc. In view of the experience of institutional operations over the past few years and the structural changes in price conditions, it is necessary to make a rational determination of the target indicators and target levels. The way monetary policy instruments are operated should also be greatly improved. We should change the operating standards of the total amount limit loan system to further strengthen the ability to support small and medium-sized enterprises in the province, and prepare fundamental measures to solve the problem of leakage of monetary stability securities as soon as possible. Everything. In addition, in view of the linkage with interest rate policy from a medium-term perspective, the overall operating system of the current loan system, the reserve payment system, and the open market manipulation system need to be reexamined . In response to the increasing volatility of the market, we must further strengthen our financial stability efforts. Financial and foreign exchange market trends should be checked at all times and if anomalies are detected, it is necessary to respond quickly by properly utilizing the functions of open market manipulation or foreign exchange transaction inspection. In addition, in order to alleviate the burden of settlement funds on financial institutions, Han should be careful not to compromise the safety of the payment system in the process of converting the payment method of the financial network from a total amount settlement to a mixed settlement of the total amount and difference. The issuance of the new currency, which is scheduled for the first half of next year, is directly related to the life of the people, so it is necessary to cooperate closely with the relevant authorities to make preparations. In addition, based on the achievements of the national economic education, it is necessary to strengthen the financial content, strengthen targeted education , and expand online education. When it comes to the management of foreign currency funds , we should continue to expand our professional workforce to match their size and actively introduce and utilize the latest investment and risk management techniques to further enhance our operational capabilities. Dear Bank of Korea Family! Now, as well as the policy environment, we must face the fact that the management environment of the party has changed greatly from the previous one. In order to adapt to the changed environment and remain competitive, there must be bold self-innovation. To this end, a plan should be taken to firmly establish a personnel management system that places personnel in the right place based on competence, and to reorganize the organization with a focus on the dramatic dialogue of work efficiency and synergy. In addition, we must establish an organizational culture that actively discusses and shares information while aiming for the harmony of competition and cooperation. At present, the "Development Committee for Medium- and Long-Term Development Strategies" has been formed to establish a vision for the future role of the party and to explore development strategies that can implement it. Based on the aforementioned basic direction of organization and personnel management, we should promptly come up with specific initiatives. We hope that the employees will also participate actively and gather the benefits. Dear Bank of Korea Family! In order for the Bank of Korea to receive the unwavering trust of the people , it must be preceded by the dedicated efforts of all its employees. Each and every employee must be the best expert in their field by constantly striving for self-development . In addition , keep in mind that the central bank staff are public servants, so that they will do their best to do their job in a manner that serves the country and society. Today, as we celebrate our 56th anniversary, let us recommit ourselves to our mission and responsibilities as central bankers. May health and happiness always be with you and your families. Thanks. 06-12-2006 President Lee Sung-tae

Title: Hamjunho Commissioner Lee Im-sa
text: Leaving the Bank of Korea Leaving the Bank of Korea 2018. 5. 11 Financial and Monetary Commissioner Ham Jun-ho Honorable Governor, Fellow Members, Employees. It seems like the last time I took office, but I am already standing here, so I am very grateful. In retrospect, the last 4 years have been a period of literal upheaval. Coming to office shortly after the Sewol issue, it was a series of heart-wrenching moments leading up to MERS, the collapse of Chinese stocks, impeachment, THAAD and the North Korean nuclear crisis, the Olympics and the North-South summit. As developed countries roll out (-) interest rate policies following quantitative easing, we have also lowered interest rates 5 times due to deteriorating growth vitality and excessive low prices, but seeing an economy that rarely responds as if pulling a loosened rope is frustrating and frustrating. I felt it. However, I am reminded of the poem of the mindset that "all the things of the world are revealed only when they are calm," and the more complex and confusing it is, the farther away it is and the more it is willing to make a decision that is in line with the essential current. I did my best to not be enough. While the ROK economy has maintained a stable flow of growth that has not significantly stripped off its potential level in the face of successive adverse events, the recent economy has shown some signs of recovery, leaving the first step in normalizing interest rates. It's a bit comforting. As you may recall, when I took office 4 years ago, the two tasks that I said I would work on with more emphasis during my term of office were "the advancement of the monetary policy operating system" and "the strengthening of the functions of financial stability." Looking back, I think there have been a lot of changes and progress in both sectors over the past 4 years. I have done a lot of work with you, but I have worked hard to establish the general principles of monetary policy operation while reducing the number of base rate decisions, to improve the policy system and strengthen communication, to enhance the function of financial stability analysis, and to have the Financial Stability Review Conference of the Gold Barrel in earnest. The back is memorable. Although I am a little embarrassed from the position of leaving, based on my experience , I would like to share a few thoughts regarding the direction of future policy operations. First, as a central bank in an open and emerging country, a structure that is bound to be heavily affected by external shocks, we are desensitizing how difficult it is to operate inflation targeting in a future-oriented manner. The current reality is that the external shocks and uncertainties affecting the growth and price path are so great that it is not easy to operate monetary policy proactively based on the outlook. Nevertheless, there is a lag before the policy effect can be realized by real inflation, so we have to look ahead and determine interest rates , and central banks in other medium-sized and open-ended developed countries whose situation is similar to ours are also exploring various ways to overcome the real difficulties . In that sense, we too will have to make unremitting efforts to ensure the continued good and internalization of the policy operating system. First of all, what our Treasury emphasized by reducing the number of interest rate decisions to 8 was the need to strengthen the link between the economic network and monetary policy, and we need to continue to expand the analysis and model infrastructure that can actually support this. By formulating and promulgating the general principles of monetary policy operations, we have already stated that we are aiming for a future-oriented policy operation that converges inflation to the target level in the medium-term clock. In the actual operation, we will also need to further internalize the analysis model and information sharing system to support policy operations that create the best price forecast path and link it to the guidelines for the adjustment of the reference rate. Although it is realistically difficult to fully implement a high-fidelity fourcast forecasting system that systematically feeds the hammer before conditional inflation and the gap with inflation targets at every rate decision, in the medium term Think far from the right inflation path that can adequately support growth and financial stability while meeting price targets within the clock, and analyze what is the optimal interest rate path to achieve this path . The approach will also need to be complementary. Second, although the policy clock of the "medium term" is recognized as around 2-3 years, it is necessary to concretely refine it. With regard to the achievement of monetary policy goals, the Bank of Korea is comprehensively empowered not only to have the independence of tools such as the management of interest rates, but also to define and interpret the criteria for achieving a given inflation target. Accordingly, it is thought that the corresponding communication should also be carried out more faithfully. As is well known, if the policy clock for meeting the price target is too short, it can lead to excessive policy response when the price target is deviated, undermining the stability of market interest rates and overestimating growth in the central bank's loss function. On the other hand, if the clock becomes too long, the continuation of the divergence from price targets will undermine the credibility of the central bank, undermining the effectiveness of monetary policy. Therefore, through a deeper discussion and analysis of the extent of the medium-term policy clock that is in line with the characteristics of our economy, we should consider using this as the basis of the spirit of policy luck and, if necessary, communicating externally. . Most central banks also seem to be running monetary policy, usually with a policy clock of 2-3 years. For example, New Zealand is internally setting a policy clock of around 3 years and trying to achieve price target convergence within that period, while Australia is currently 'by gones' are focusing on 'convergence' on price targets. Taking a step forward from the by gones' approach, the medium-term average inflation target method, which seeks to bring the inflation rate average of around 5 years closer to the target, is also known to be experimenting with as a precursor to price level targeting. With the Fed, the ECB, and the Bank of Japan also offering prices and growth paths for the next 3 years, a policy clock of about 3 years seems useful. In our case, we are supposed to reset the price target every 3 years, but this is a target reset cycle, and the appropriate policy clock needs to be determined to reflect the parallax structure of monetary policy or the persistence of supply shocks. As we continue to explore how many policy clocks are more suitable for our price process, we will have to consider ways to expand the forecast clock for prices and growth paths to this level. In addition, as long as the price target is set at CPI rather than the source price, and the impact of supply shocks affecting the CPI inflation rate, etc. are analyzed in more detail, the optimal path to achieve the price target within the policy clock under the given economic conditions at the time of each policy decision and We will have to explore ways to efficiently communicate the convergence rate to economic actors. The prolongation of this policy and forecast clock should enhance policy confidence and improve growth or financial stability by making economic actors understand that even if the inflation rate is outside 2% for a certain period of time, the goal should not be achieved annually depending on the duration of the supply shock, etc. I think it will also help us to flexibly incorporate it into monetary policy operations. Third, in this process, it is necessary to continue efforts to develop various models and expand the analysis system so that financial stability risks can be systematically reversed in the operation of appropriate monetary policy. I personally believe that macroprudential policy should be the primary defense of financial stability, but I also believe that monetary policy changes financial stability risks and, again, the ripple effects of financial stability risks on medium- to long-term growth and prices cannot be overlooked. Therefore, I have posited the decision of interest rates as a process of my constrained optimization that constrains financial stability risks. As a result , the judgment and consideration of financial stability risks is directly related to how fast or how flexibly prices will be brought closer to the target level . Furthermore, the effective upper and lower limits of interest rate management will ultimately be determined by the country's financial stability or shock-absorbing capabilities. The problem is that the critical level of acceptable financial stability risk is a time-variable variable determined by interaction with other relevant policies, such as macroprudential policies, real estate policies, etc., in addition to basic economic conditions. It adds to the Spirit's challenges. In the end, it can only be a qualitative judgment, but it would be very desirable if a more diverse set of models and approaches could effectively support decisions like this. On the other hand, it is necessary to make it more clear what it means to consider financial stability in the operation of monetary policy. If we consider the risk of leakage of household debt here, we are not arguing that we should look at financial stability risk indicators, such as the debt-to-benefit ratio, as another intermediate tagget variable in monetary policy when it comes to determining interest rates. Rather, in the longer term we can see how the path of household debt, which is bound to be affected by the interest rate path, will affect future growth and price pathways through changes in household balance sheets, changes in house prices, and even the possibility of a financial crisis. It's something you have to consider. Since the financial history cycle is usually longer than the physical cycle, this analysis needs to be done on a longer clock than the conventional monetary policy clock mentioned above. For example, in selecting the target price path of the medium-term policy clock mentioned above, it is necessary to combine the analysis on a longer clock to determine how the management of the reference rate to achieve this price path correlates with key financial stability indicators such as household debt ratios and DSRs in the future . Yes. Furthermore, like the central banks of the Northern Europe, it is necessary to try to simulate on a longer clock how interest rate adjustments and the consequent changes in the credit cycle can be linked to the probability of a future financial crisis or asset price adjustment, while also trying to navigate the right rate path . Yes. In addition, in view of the fact that the impact of the financial cycle on the real water economy is greater than one might think, and therefore, many studies have suggested that monetary policy that takes into account financial imbalances may be superior in terms of maximizing economic welfare. I think we should continue to internalize the ripple path and related macroeconomic models. Finally, apart from the operation of monetary policy, it is necessary to continue to expand the functions related to the macroprudence policy of the Bank of Korea. I believe that the macroprudential policy of our country has been properly established We believe that the fundamental cornerstone for its operation is the timely and neutral financial stability risk assessment function of the party. In this sense, I believe that the Financial Stability Conference, which has been upgraded to the plenary session of the Gold Barrel Committee since last year, and the resulting Financial Stability Report, are one of the most important macroprudential policy instruments. While it is true that the quality of the financial stability report has improved in terms of content, the risk assessment section needs to be further expanded. This risk assessment includes a more in-depth system lease It goes without saying that it must be supported by the ability to analyze the craziness. Sector-specific, static financial stability analysis and derivative financial stability analysis that rely on post-mortem indicators such as financial statements, delinquency rates, and credit growth rates of financial institutions, and how financial institutions, markets, and commodity areas are linked across the street from a more systemic point of view, and from a dynamic point of view, What is the endogenous path of transition of risk, what interactions arise with the real economy, real estate, and the global liquidity cycle, and whether we have the spontaneous resilience to absorb and tolerate the shocks that accumulate in the process , etc. We will continue to expand our macroscopic system risk analysis capabilities, which differentiate it from the risk analysis on the side. Many of the tasks mentioned above are those that you have already been thinking about for a lot of time and are working on improving in practice. I believe that the human resources and potential of our Bank of Korea are never second to those of advanced central banks. As we all know, our economy faces fundamental challenges, including aging and low births, inefficiencies in the capital and job markets, declining productivity due to delays in restructuring, polarization and leakage of household debt. Against the backdrop of unprecedented monetary easing and debt expansion, it remains uncertain how sustainable the recent global economic recovery will be. In the midst of rapidly changing external conditions, with the urgency of productivity and social integration in response to aging and polarization, the need for correct policy formulation based on objective statistics and rigorous analysis is higher than ever. The central bank is the best person to move away from short-sightedness and perform in-depth, neutral research and analysis functions. As the status and role of the party has become so great, I ask all of you to gather your wisdom and devote yourself more fully to the role of the invading and the invasion of our economy so that our economy can cruise in the face of harsh winds. I am now returning to my college campus. A history that I read as a child without knowing what it meant Just as I have seen the philosophy book again with age and realized its true intention, I think I will now be able to give lectures and research that I can do with my own integrity. The moments I have pondered and discussed with you so much will be cherished as the honor of my life. And based on this experience, we will also help the Bank of Korea to reach out to the point where it is necessary and helpful to operate the monetary credit policy of our country from the outside. Mr. Governor, Vice Governor, fellow committee members, and employees and reporters who have prepared and joined me in preparing this for me today, once again, I am deeply grateful for the warm consideration and repatriation of many of you. .

Title: Macrofinancial Linkages and Policy Implications
Subtitle: BOK-BIS-IMF Conference
text: Macrofinancial Linkages and Policy Implications Choongsoo Kim Governor Bank of Korea BOK-BIS-IMF Conference April 10, 2012, Seoul, Korea Good morning. I would like to extend my warmest welcome to all participants from central banks, supervisory agencies, international organizations, academia and finance around the world, attending this BOK-BIS-IMF Joint Conference. My special thanks go to Stephen Cecchetti, Director of BIS, Jan Brockmeijer, Deputy Director of the IMF, and David Fernandez, Managing Director of JP Morgan, who have set aside their valuable time to be with us here despite the pressures of their busy schedules. I also would like to express my gratitude to the staff members of the BIS (Ben Cohen, Frank Packer), and of the IMF (Scott Roger, Andre Oliveira Santos), who were responsible for the preparation of this conference, and to all the moderators, presenters and panelists. Macrofinancial Linkages and Policy Implications, the theme for this conference, is of vital importance, embracing a wide range of issues that must be considered in striving to prevent the recurrence of the financial crisis in the future. In the central banks and supervisory agencies of individual countries, international organizations and the academic world, a wide range of studies have been undertaken for some time concerning macrofinancial linkages, and significant progress has been made. Particularly, there has been a substantial 1 / 20 advance in these studies as the foundation has now been laid for an in-depth understanding of the influence of such linkages on the economic system as a whole. A notable step in this has been the establishment of a basis for systemic analyses through the construction of a macroeconomic model that includes the financial sector. This conference consequently gives us the valuable opportunity to collate the results of the research so far and to set what needs to be done in future. In this regard, I would like to talk about a change in the perception of macrofinancial linkages, the direction of the international communitys policy response to global financial crises, and their implications. Change in Perception of Macrofinancial Linkages before and after the Global Financial Crisis The global financial crisis in 2008 acted to bring about a change in the existing perception that individual countries policy authorities, academics, and financial practitioners had about the interlinkages running between the real economy and the financial sector. Recognition before the Crisis 2 / 20 From the mid-1980s until the global financial crisis in 2008, the economies of major countries around the world experienced low and stable inflation and stable economic growth for a long time, maintaining what was termed the Great Moderation.1 In this process, the policy authorities and the academic world shared the view that central banks should focus on price stability through for instance inflation targeting, and that the policy objective of all governments in moderating economic volatility should be to manage sovereign debt in line with policy objectives, rather than that the governments of individual countries implement fiscal policies in a discretionary manner. 2 Along with this, it was generally agreed that market principles were working nearly perfectly with financial market participants effectively using market information and that new financial products developed through financial innovation, including ABS and derivatives, could be used as effective tools for risk diversification.3 There is a view that this pre-crisis confidence in the completeness of market functions was based on the Effective Markets Hypothesis advocated by Eugene Fama 4 and other economists. Accordingly, discussions on macrofinancial linkages did not gain particular attention. As you are well aware, 1 James Stock and Mark Watson, Has the Business Cycle Changed and Why?, NBER Macroeconomics Annual 2002, Volume 17, 159-230, 2002. 2 Oliver Blanchard, Giovanni DellAriccia, and Paolo Mauro, Rethinking Macroeconomic Policy, IMF Staff Position Note, 12 February 2010. 3 ECB, The Incentive Structure of the Originate and Distribute Model, December 2008. 4 Eugene Fama, Efficient Capital Markets: A Review of Theory and Empirical Work, Journal of Finance, Vol. 25, No. 2, 383-417, 1970. 3 / 20 the efficient markets hypothesis assumes that participants in the financial market acquire and utilize all the information publicly available in the market, making prices of financial assets always converge to an equilibrium. However, the hypothesis has some problems  it excludes the possibility that the financial sector could cause endogenous instability, and also neglects the possibility of unreasonable judgment by economic agents, as assumed by behavioral finance, which is currently gaining increasing attention. Changed Perception after the Crisis Even before the crisis, research had been conducted in some areas on the effect of the financial sector on the real economy, taking an assumption of the incompleteness of financial markets. For example, the financial accelerator model presented by Ben Bernanke5 and others raises the possibility that asymmetries of information between fund providers and users could shrink credit supply, and have a negative impact on the real economy. Moreover, Minsky also warns that Ponzi financing, which arises from excessive risk seeking in the process of corporate fund raising in economic upturns, could cause financial unrest, and he also mentions the inherent instability of the financial sector. 6 5 Ben Bernanke, Mark Gertler and Simon Gilchrist, The Financial Accelerator and the Flight to Quality, Review of Economics and Statistics, Vol. 78, No. 1, 1-15, February 1996. 6 Hyman Minsky, The Financial Instability Hypothesis, Jerome Levy Economics Institute Working Paper, No. 74, May 1992. 4 / 20 Since the global financial crisis, however, the importance of research on macrofinancial linkages has again come to the fore; specifically the process by which financial sector instability, caused by financial market incompleteness resulting mainly from asymmetries of information, greatly affects the real economy, and this influence feeds back once again to the financial sector. This change in awareness was also largely brought about by the experience of witnessing the mutually non-linear and unstable relationship between the real economy and the financial sector 7 being effectively realized due to procyclicality, which leads the financial sector to expand excessively during economic upturns and shrink too fiercely during economic downturns. Policy Responses of the International Community to Prevent another Crisis Along with the change in the understanding of the macrofinancial linkages, the global community has come up with various policy response measures to overcome and prevent crises, and these measures focus on the reform of 7 BIS, Addressing financial system procyclicality: a possible framework, Note for the FSF Working Group on Market and Institutional Resilience, 2008. Ben Bernanke, The Financial Crisis and Community Banking, Speech at the Independent Community Bankers of America's National Convention and Techworld, Phoenix, Arizona, 20 March 2009. 5 / 20 financial regulation and restructuring of the supervisory system, the international financial system and economic recovery. Reform of Financial Regulation and Restructuring of Supervisory System The BCBS set up the Basel  banking regulatory framework in December 2010, in consideration of the fact that the excessive expansion of leverage by financial institutions and lack of liquidity served to trigger the financial crisis. As you know, Basel  steps up capital adequacy regulation and introduces liquidity and leverage regulations to heighten the shock absorption capacity of banks, curb excessive risk-seeking activities and ease pro-cyclicality. The BCBS plans to impose a capital surcharge on SIBs to regulate the expanded scale and interconnectedness of banks. Based on the reflection that up until the crisis, supervisory authorities focused solely on microprudential supervision related to individual financial institutions, consequently neglecting to identify and respond to systemic risks, the global trend is for the ongoing restructuring of national financial supervisory frameworks to be undertaken in such a way as to strengthen the macroprudential supervisory functions. The establishment of the FSOC in the US, the FPC in the UK, and the ESRB in the EU are examples of strengthening macroprudential supervisory functions within individual systems in the wake of the crisis. Koreas move to revise the Bank of Korea Act in August 2011 and grant the 6 / 20 Bank of Korea a financial stability mandate that calls on it to play a more proactive role in financial stability can also be seen to have reflected this global trend. Reform of International Financial System Under the current international financial system, there is a strong likelihood that the global imbalances could persist. In this regard, there are concerns in the international community that unless response measures to resolve them are swiftly put in place, there is a risk that the global financial crisis could recur. To spell it out, there is a heightened possibility that financial unrest could be triggered as the real sector imbalances accumulated by the macroeconomic stance in advanced economies and savings patterns in emerging market economies are transmitted to the financial sector, and that this could spread rapidly to emerging market economies8 whose net capital flow volatility is relatively greater than that in advanced economies. In line with this, the G20 has recently agreed on the introduction of Coherent Conclusions to ease capital flow volatility, and concerning the GFSN, it recognized the importance of central banks role, such as the conclusion of currency swap arrangements among central banks in responding to a liquidity crisis and supported the introduction of the IMFs Precautionary Liquidity 8 IMF, World Economic Outlook, Chapter 4, April 2011. 7 / 20 Line.9 Apart from this, systems for mitigating capital flow volatility have been established in individual countries. Koreas imposition of ceilings on banks FX forward positions and the Macroprudential Stability Levy on non-deposit foreign liabilities in October 2010 and August 2011 respectively, is also a case in point. Implementation of Policy Responses for Economic Recovery In the aftermath of the global financial crisis, countries around the world have carried out monetary and fiscal policies to preclude, in the course of overcoming the crisis, the setting in motion of a vicious cycle by which yet another crisis is triggered due to a delay in economic recovery.10 Central banks have cut their benchmark rates to a great extent, and some of them in advanced nations have implemented monetary easing through largescale Treasury bond purchases as policy rates have been cut to the zero level.11 While the US Federal Reserve undertook two Large-Scale Asset Purchases (LSAP) of Treasury bonds after the crisis, it also bought and sold both short and long term Treasury bonds for economic recovery. The BOE and the ECB 9 2011 G20 Cannes Summit, November 2011. 10 Tamim Bayoumi and Ola Melander, Credit Matter: Empirical Evidence on U.S. Macro-Financial Linkages, Working Paper 169, IMF, 2008. 11 Jack Meaning and Feng Zhu, The impact of recent central bank asset purchase programmes, BIS Quarterly Review, BIS, December 2011. 8 / 20 similarly provided massive funds to the banking sector through the Asset Purchase Facility (APF) and the expansion of RP transactions (LTRO).12 Along with this, certain individual governments have pushed ahead with expansionary fiscal policies to boost the economy, and focused on fiscal spending such as SOC investment whose economic stimulus effects are realized over the short run, rather than on tax cuts whose effects only work through after some time lag. To soothe the financial turmoil quickly at the early stage of crisis, they also substantially increased fiscal inputs to ensure financial market stability in terms of financial institutions recapitalization, debt guarantees, asset purchases, liquidity provision and the like. Policy Implications The recent global financial crisis was triggered by shocks that were mutually amplified between the real and financial sectors i.e. macrofinancial linkages. This demonstrated that the effectiveness of traditional monetary, fiscal and financial stability policies is reduced in a crisis. To prevent another crisis and promote stable and balanced growth in the real sector, we need therefore to 12 Although using RP transactions with maturity of one week, two weeks, and one month in its main refinancing operations (MRO), the ECB uses three-month RP transactions in its longer-term refinancing operations (LTRO), originally introduced for additional fund supply to the banking sector in 2003, and it also commenced 6-, 12-, 36-month RP transactions after the global financial crisis. 9 / 20 continue discussions on a new policy paradigm, including the macroprudential policy framework, and this calls for a consensus to be reached within the international community. Balanced Operation of Monetary and Macroprudential Policies As has been borne out by the current crisis, we need to take on board the point that it is hard to achieve real sector stability by seeking price stability alone without the pursuit at the same time of financial stability. 13 Although appropriate monetary policy responses are called for to achieve price and financial stability, monetary policy does not always affect price and financial stability in the same direction. With this in mind, we should recognize the importance of supplementing monetary policy with macroprudential policy in achieving the two policy goals.14 In line with this, the ongoing discussion in the international community on Lean vs. Clean gives us very important insights. The clean approach argues that, since it is difficult to identify real estate price bubbles in advance, policy responses based on asset prices at some theoretical equilibrium may increase 13 Meanwhile, before the global financial crisis, there was implicit agreement in academia that price stability serves as a necessary factor for real economic growth, preventing excessive investment and enhancing economic efficiency, and that a central bank should therefore strive to ensure price stability.(Frederic S. Mishkin, What Should Central Banks Do?, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis Review 82(6), 1-14, 2000) 14 Oliver Blanchard, Giovanni DellAriccia, and Paolo Mauro, Rethinking Macroeconomic Policy, IMF Staff Position Note, 12 February 2010. 10 / 20 macroeconomic instability, and hence it would rather be appropriate to clean troubled assets after these bubbles burst of their own accord. The lean approach, on the other hand, insists that, since dead-weight losses from burst bubbles have been soaring owing to the growing interconnectedness of financial markets, the central bank should give attention to financial stability as well as to price stability by picking up quickly on a surge in asset prices and responding to it ahead of time, rather than sticking to benign neglect.15 The case for the lean approach is becoming more compelling, boosted by an increasing number of studies that add a bank lending channel (or credit-supply channel) to the borrowers balance-sheet channel (or collateral channel) of the financial accelerator model proposed by Bernanke and others. Among the papers to be presented during this conference, the argument by Gambacorta and Signoretti16 has important implications for central banks. They argue that the costs can be significantly reduced in terms of macroeconomic stability if the scope of monetary policy is widened to include variables for macroprudential policy, such as asset prices and aggregate credit. 15 William White, Should Monetary Policy Lean or Clean?, Globalization and Monetary Policy Institute Working Paper No. 34, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, 2009. 16 Leonardo Gambacorta and Federico M. Signoretti, Should monetary policy lean against the wind? An analysis based on a DSGE model with banking, BOK/BIS/IMF Conference, April 2012. 11 / 20 Along with this, the governance structure of macroprudential policies is crucial in order to prevent coordination failure in the implementation of monetary and macroprudential policies and for the balanced operation of these two policies.17 In this regard, the central bank needs to take on responsibility for financial stability and play its role as one of the policy authorities carrying out macroprudential policy. Development of Policy Measures in Response to the Possibility of an Increase in the Volatility of Capital Flows Amid persistent concerns about global imbalances, it is urgent for emerging market countries to develop their own policy measures in response to an increase in the volatility of capital flows. To this end, they need to keep their short-term external liabilities and foreign reserves at appropriate levels, while working toward the stable operation of the macroeconomy. Korea can be cited as a good example of a drive to lessen the volatility of capital flows by making use of macroprudential policy tools. Given that global liquidity has been increasing as countries around the world have implemented monetary easing in the course of addressing the crisis, and that financial markets' interconnectedness has been strengthening, global 17 Thomas J. Jordan, The Interaction of Monetary and Macropuential Policy, Conference on Future of Central Banking under Globalization, Bank of Japan, 27 May 2010. 12 / 20 financial cooperation should be stepped up to prevent capital flows from causing financial instability. In so far as we lack a global jurisdiction that regulates the already globalized financial markets, we should constantly strive to facilitate international policy bodies, such as the G20, to achieve global policy coordination through close international cooperation.18 Discussion on Achieving Global Equilibrium to Prevent Recurrence of Crisis If the euro area sovereign debt crisis persists and the recovery of the real economy is delayed worldwide, a vicious circle may be set in motion in which the aftereffects of one global financial crisis trigger another. Considering the macrofinancial linkages, economic instability would then persist unless the imbalances between the real and financial sectors were resolved. From this perspective, efforts are required to get the world economy back on track. However, there is some scepticism as to whether in continuing the current approach we can reach a sustained and stable global equilibrium and break free from a vicious cycle of crisis. A local equilibrium can be achieved if large-scale quantitative easing and liquidity provision for instance by the IMF are concentrated on some regions of the world, more specifically on European 18 From this perspective, a policy actor capable of managing global liquidity is needed, and the creation of an International Monetary Policy Committee (IMPC), mooted in academia, sounds very promising. 13 / 20 countries. On the other hand, this would increase the possibility of negative spillover effects on other regions, such as Asian emerging countries, leading to multiple equilibria, in which good and bad equilibria coexist. Resolution of the global financial crisis ultimately depends on the recovery of the entire world economy. In this respect, to achieve global equilibrium, the international community should strive to bring this about by boosting investment in the Asian emerging market countries that now spearhead world economic growth. Concluding Remarks The world economy has been experiencing the worst global financial crisis since the Great Depression. The criticism that we are now faced with a crisis in economics as well as an economic crisis spooks us, when we simply try to address the current crisis on the basis of our previous experience and knowledge. As the global financial system is going through fundamental structural changes caused by strengthened financial market interconnectedness and financial innovation, there is a steady increase in those things that cannot be explained by the simplified macroeconomic models of economic orthodoxy. In this regard, at this BOK-BIS-IMF joint-conference, we are set to witness attempts to explain new economic phenomena in a different, progressive light rather than the traditional perspective of the broad economic consensus. 14 / 20 In his famous book titled The Grand Design, Stephen Hawking argues that there is no single theory that can explain various physical phenomena at the same time.19 Likewise, there are limitations to analyzing various and complex phenomena in the current global economic system with simplified models. This conference allows us a chance to make a significant attempt to overcome such difficulties that current economics faces. While looking over the papers to be presented at this conference, I did notice that they were all co-authored by writers from central banks, supervisory authorities, international organizations and academia. This also implies that, in order to cope with the complex economic reality, we should not depend solely on the insights of a single writer, as was previously the norm, and that people from the policy-making and academic fields should work together to establish a framework for research and analysis and come up with measures in response. As I mentioned earlier, the lean approach, which adds the credit-supply side to the existing DSGE model to consider financial stability, has proved to make a greater contribution to price and real economic stability.20 This is an example of a different argument that parts company with the conventional consensus, 19 Stephen Hawking and Leonard Mlodinow, But just as there is no flat map that is a good representation of the earths entire surface, there is no single theory that is a good representation of observations in all situations., Remark from The Grand Design, Bantam, 2010. 20 Leonardo Gambacortaand Federico M. Signoretti, op. cit. 15 / 20 and one that has been inspired by the change in our understanding of economic phenomena since the crisis. Moreover, in an attempt to enrich agent heterogeneity on the existing models, economists in the vanguard added a shadow banking system to the existing banking sector21 and assumed households to be heterogeneous economic agents by sorting them based on their degree of durable and non-durable endowment. All this can be seen as part of the efforts to analyze the complexities of the financial system with macroeconomic models. The macroeconomic models to be discussed at this conference are expected to be applicable not only to structural problems of the current economic system in which heterogeneous economic agents emerge as a result of social polarization, but also to the problems arising from country-specific economic forms, which are basically divided into large closed economies and small open economies. Nobody would have expected that central banks would continue to maintain the unconventional monetary policy of quantitative easing for such a long time, in order to bring about a recovery from the aftershocks of Lehman Brothers collapse in 2008.22 Nowadays, unconventional policy tools such as the QE of the U.S. Fed, the APF of the Bank of England and the LTRO of the ECB have 21 Charles A. E. Goodhart, Anil K Kashyap, Dimitrios P. Tsomocos and Alexandros P. Vardoulakis, Financial Regulation in General Equilibrium, BOK/BIS/IMF Conference, April 2012. 22 Jean-Claude Trichet, Nobody would have expected such a long time after Lehman Brothers, [central banks] would continue to have this level of expansion of our balance sheets, Remark from Trichet warns of nations behavioral contagion, MarketWatch , 24 March 2012. 16 / 20 been thrust into sharp relief. Thus, it is high time for us to be able to predict the unintended consequences of these policy tools and to be prepared for them. Since major countries measures to reform financial regulations, including Basel  of the BCBS, focus mostly on the prevention of crisis recurrence, we need to continuously monitor and track how these measures will affect the sustainability of world economic growth in the medium- and long-term. In this regard, we should be careful so that the strengthening of financial regulation does not weaken the benign function of finance, which is to drive the growth of the real economy through seamless financial intermediation. Moreover, in todays more closely interconnected world economy, the strengthening of financial regulation with a primary focus on advanced countries does not equally affect the financial system in emerging market countries with their significantly different financial structure. In this regard, in examining the implementation of regulations, an in-depth analysis should be conducted of how these regulations will affect the financial industries of emerging market countries and all other countries other than the advanced economies, and their careful monitoring is called for. At this critical juncture where the role of central banks is being established anew and close attention should be paid to the effects of financial regulatory reforms, in-depth studies and discussions on macrofinancial linkages will make a meaningful contribution to central banks and related policy authorities in 17 / 20 setting and implementing policies to achieve balanced and stable economic growth. Among those studies underway so far, I think that greater concentration is called for on in-depth studies as to the impact of the increased volatility of cross-border capital flows on the business cycle through credit channels. In addition, further research would also be beneficial on how shocks generated endogenously in the financial sector affect the real economy.23 Moreover, more research is needed to develop macroeconomic models that incorporate financial friction, macrofinancial nonlinearities, structural instabilities and financial market interconnectedness.24 The tasks that I have just mentioned do not of course include all the issues that have a bearing on the study of macrofinancial linkages. However, I hope that they will serve as a good starting point for discussions during this Conference and as a basis for stepping up the tempo of research on macrofinancial linkages.
